name: Azimuth reference mapping
summary: Maps query cells onto annotated Seurat references (PBMC, lung, kidney and others) by supervised PCA and anchors, returning labels at several levels with prediction and mapping scores
caveats: Labels and resolution are those of the reference; query-only states map to the nearest reference type, so the mapping score should be checked. No independent peer-reviewed benchmark found.
cite_title: Integrated analysis of multimodal single-cell data.
publication_title: Integrated analysis of multimodal single-cell data.

name: Seurat weighted nearest neighbours (WNN)
summary: Learns per-cell weights for each modality from how well it predicts its neighbours, and builds one weighted nearest-neighbour graph for joint clustering, UMAP and reference mapping of CITE-seq or multiome data
gain: Hu 2024: Seurat, MOJITOO and scAI led vertical (same-cell) integration across 47 datasets (abstract); the Seurat run there was WNN (FindMultiModalNeighbors in Seurat 4.3.0.1 for RNA+ADT and RNA+ATAC, per the authors' code); Hao 2021 built a 211,000-cell, 228-antibody PBMC reference with it (self-reported)
caveats: Modality weights reflect neighbourhood consistency, so a noisy, unnormalised ADT panel or ATAC with few fragments simply gets down-weighted rather than flagged
cite_title: Integrated analysis of multimodal single-cell data.
publication_title: Integrated analysis of multimodal single-cell data.

name: Seurat anchor integration (CCA and RPCA)
summary: Identifies anchor pairs of mutual nearest neighbours in a shared canonical correlation (or reciprocal PCA) space and uses them to correct expression or transfer labels between datasets
gain: Tran 2020: Seurat 3 among the three recommended methods of 14 (with Harmony and LIGER)
caveats: scIB ranked Seurat v3 CCA and RPCA below scANVI, Scanorama, scVI and scGen on atlas tasks; the same anchor framework underlies Azimuth label transfer.
cite_title: Comprehensive Integration of Single-Cell Data.
publication_title: Comprehensive Integration of Single-Cell Data.

name: Empirical Bayes moderation (limma, edgeR QL, DESeq2/apeglm)
summary: Shrink gene-wise variances, dispersions or fold changes toward a trend estimated across all genes, so tests with 2-3 replicates borrow residual degrees of freedom from the whole transcriptome
recovers: Stable variance and effect estimates when each condition has very few replicates
caveats: Borrows across genes, not across conditions or drugs; assumes most genes follow a shared variance trend. It cannot create replication: with zero residual degrees of freedom there is nothing to moderate. edgeR v4 revised the quasi-likelihood treatment for small counts, relevant to pseudobulks of few cells.
cite_title: Linear models and empirical bayes methods for assessing differential expression in microarray experiments.
publication_title: Linear models and empirical bayes methods for assessing differential expression in microarray experiments.
publication_venue: Statistical Applications in Genetics and Molecular Biology

name: Harmony
summary: Iteratively clusters cells in PCA space and applies cluster-specific linear corrections that maximise batch diversity within clusters, returning a corrected embedding
gain: Tran 2020: recommended first among 14 methods (with LIGER and Seurat 3) for its accuracy and much shorter runtime; scIB: among the best four on the human immune task and effective on scATAC-seq
caveats: Returns an embedding, not corrected counts; scIB found it weaker than scANVI, Scanorama and scVI on complex atlas tasks.
cite_title: Fast, sensitive and accurate integration of single-cell data with Harmony.
publication_title: Fast, sensitive and accurate integration of single-cell data with Harmony.

name: LISI (local inverse Simpson's index)
summary: Effective number of batches (iLISI) or cell types (cLISI) in each cell's neighbourhood, introduced with Harmony
caveats: Like kBET, cannot tell batch effect from batch-specific cell types without labels; one of the scIB metrics.
cite_title: Fast, sensitive and accurate integration of single-cell data with Harmony
publication_title: Fast, sensitive and accurate integration of single-cell data with Harmony

name: Cell Ranger (cellranger count / multi)
summary: 10x Genomics pipeline that aligns reads with STAR, corrects barcodes and UMIs against the kit whitelist, counts UMIs per gene and calls cells, producing the raw and filtered matrices most 10x analyses start from
recovers: a reproducible, vendor-supported count matrix; low-RNA cells through its EmptyDrops-style second calling step
gain: You 2021 (10 workflows, mixtures with known labels): performance "consistently high and relatively stable", among the top 3 on one downstream ranking; Bruning 2022: gene sets similar to STARsolo and alevin-fry
caveats: Slowest of the common pipelines (STARsolo, alevin and kallisto >= 3x faster, kallisto 4-6x, Bruning 2022). Counts only sense reads confidently assigned to one gene, so gene-ambiguous reads are dropped. Calls cells by an order-of-magnitude UMI cut (m/10 of the 99th percentile of the expected top barcodes) followed by EmptyDrops for low-RNA barcodes, with a bounded candidate set (see [[emptydrops]]). Intronic reads counted by default from v7.0, which changes counts and calls compared with earlier versions. Outside human and mouse its extra cells were mostly low quality (Shainer 2021).
cite_title: Massively parallel digital transcriptional profiling of single cells
publication_title: Massively parallel digital transcriptional profiling of single cells

name: Leiden community detection
summary: Graph community detection that refines Louvain partitions so every community is guaranteed to be internally connected; the default clustering on the kNN graph in scanpy and an option in Seurat
gain: In the authors' tests up to 25% of Louvain communities were badly connected and up to 16% disconnected; Leiden guarantees connected communities and ran faster (self-reported, benchmark and real-world networks, not single-cell data)
caveats: Resolution sets the number of clusters; no independent single-cell benchmark of Leiden against Louvain was found.
cite_title: From Louvain to Leiden: guaranteeing well-connected communities.
publication_title: From Louvain to Leiden: guaranteeing well-connected communities.

name: SingleR
summary: Labels each cell by Spearman correlation with bulk or single-cell reference profiles over marker genes, iteratively fine-tuning among the top-scoring labels
gain: Abdelaal 2019: among the top five of 22 classifiers at the deeper brain annotation and in unaligned pancreas inter-dataset tests, with almost no unlabelled cells; SVM was best overall
caveats: No rejection option in the version tested; slowest method in Abdelaal 2019 (over 39 h on Zheng 68K with SingleR 0.2.2; the later Bioconductor reimplementation is much faster).
cite_title: Reference-based analysis of lung single-cell sequencing reveals a transitional profibrotic macrophage.
publication_title: Reference-based analysis of lung single-cell sequencing reveals a transitional profibrotic macrophage.

name: Seurat CellCycleScoring / scanpy score_genes_cell_cycle
summary: Scores S and G2/M marker sets (Tirosh 2016 lists) against control genes and assigns each cell to G1, S or G2M by the larger score; the default in Seurat and scanpy tutorials
gain: Guo & Chen 2024: no method consistently best across four datasets with experimental phase labels; marker-gene scoring accurate only when the marker list suits the data
caveats: Always assigns every cell to a phase, so non-cycling cells are forced into G1, S or G2M (Guo & Chen 2024); CycleMix authors report it labels mature neurons as cycling on droplet data; human gene lists need conversion for mouse.
cite_title: Dissecting the multicellular ecosystem of metastatic melanoma by single-cell RNA-seq
publication_title: Dissecting the multicellular ecosystem of metastatic melanoma by single-cell RNA-seq

name: DoubletFinder
summary: Scores each cell by the fraction of artificial doublets (averaged random cell pairs) among its nearest neighbours in PC space, with a parameter sweep (pK) chosen from the data
recovers: cleaner clusters and DE results; singlets otherwise lost to a high-UMI cap
gain: Xi & Li 2021: highest mean AUPRC (0.537) on 16 real datasets with annotated doublets, top method on the most datasets and across simulated settings, among the most robust at removing spurious clusters; Ttoouli 2025: among the top three by clustering quality after removal
caveats: Slower than cxds or Scrublet and less stable across subsamples (Xi & Li 2021); misclassified more singlets than scds, scDblFinder or Scrublet in pooled PBMC data (Demuxafy 2024); mean AUPRC 0.13-0.34 for all detectors on lineage-barcoded cell-line data (singletCode 2024); targets heterotypic doublets and needs the expected doublet rate as input.
cite_title: DoubletFinder: Doublet Detection in Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Data Using Artificial Nearest Neighbors
publication_title: DoubletFinder: Doublet Detection in Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Data Using Artificial Nearest Neighbors

name: sci-RNA-seq3
summary: Three-level single-cell combinatorial indexing of fixed nuclei (reverse-transcription, ligation and PCR barcodes) that scales exponentially with plate size
recovers: cells per experiment at a reagent cost near one cent per cell; reverse-transcription wells act as sample barcodes
gain: About 2 million nuclei from 61 mouse embryos in one experiment (2019); optimised protocol (Martin 2023): reagent cost about 1 cent per cell or less, DSP/methanol fixation gives more UMIs than paraformaldehyde, and new buffers reduce nuclei loss during washes
caveats: Historically lower sensitivity than droplet kits; collision rate is set by nuclei per final well; nuclear input under-represents cytoplasmic transcripts; lab protocol that needs liquid handling and optimisation
cite_title: The single-cell transcriptional landscape of mammalian organogenesis
publication_title: The single-cell transcriptional landscape of mammalian organogenesis

name: sctransform
summary: Regularised negative binomial regression of each gene on sequencing depth whose Pearson residuals replace log-normalised values and rank variable genes
gain: pipeComp: best separability of subpopulations and the strongest removal of library-size and detection-rate effects among normalisations tested; Ahlmann-Eltze 2023: Pearson residuals as good as, not better than, the shifted log
caveats: Lause 2021 showed the original model is overspecified and its per-gene overdispersion biased; v2 (Choudhary and Satija 2022) changed the overdispersion handling. Its residual-based regression of covariates such as mito fraction inherits pipeComp's finding that regressing out covariates hurt clustering.
cite_title: Normalization and variance stabilization of single-cell RNA-seq data using regularized negative binomial regression.
publication_title: Normalization and variance stabilization of single-cell RNA-seq data using regularized negative binomial regression.

name: velocyto (RNA velocity)
summary: Introduced RNA velocity: counts spliced and unspliced reads per gene and fits a steady-state model of splicing kinetics to predict each cell's future state
gain: Wu 2026 recommended Velocyto among five methods balancing core performance and scalability; Luo 2026 found its agreement declined significantly in downsamples
caveats: The steady-state assumption fails for transient states (motivation for scVelo's dynamical model); results depend on how reads are assigned to spliced, unspliced and ambiguous (Soneson 2021)
cite_title: RNA velocity of single cells.
publication_title: RNA velocity of single cells.

name: Dose-response modelling across doses
summary: Model each gene or program score as a function of dose (a log-dose term in a GLM, or sigmoid and benchmark-dose curves) so all doses of a drug inform one trend instead of being tested one at a time
recovers: Power from doses that are individually underpowered; potency summaries (EC50-like) per drug
gain: sci-Plex: generalized linear regression on dose found 6,238 genes with dose-dependent expression in at least one of three cell lines (FDR < 5%) at a median of 100-200 cells per condition
caveats: A monotone or log-linear dose term misses non-monotone responses; TRADE found perturbations whose responses differ qualitatively across dose levels. Cell-level dose regression is still pseudoreplicated unless doses are crossed with replicate wells. Bulk comparison in sci-Plex showed weaker agreement for small effects. See [[sci-plex]].
cite_title: Dose-Response Analysis Using R.
publication_title: Dose-Response Analysis Using R.
citation_note: 1 listed paper(s) had no citation count

name: Slingshot
summary: Infers branching lineages by fitting a minimum spanning tree over clusters and then simultaneous principal curves, returning one pseudotime per lineage
gain: Saelens 2019: highest overall accuracy score of all evaluated methods (0.706, then PAGA Tree 0.695 and SCORPIUS 0.672) in the authors' results data from February 2019, two months before publication, where it was also first on the combined accuracy, scalability, stability and usability score; in the 29-method preprint it was the only method good across most trajectory types
caveats: Works on a reduced dimension and a clustering supplied by the user, so cluster-level artefacts (doublet clusters, stress clusters) become lineage nodes; doublets created spurious branches in Xi and Li 2021. The Saelens rank is read from the authors' results file (github dynverse/dynbenchmark_results, 08-summary/results.rds) because the published text is paywalled
cite_title: Slingshot: cell lineage and pseudotime inference for single-cell transcriptomics.
publication_title: Slingshot: cell lineage and pseudotime inference for single-cell transcriptomics.
qc_links: doublets:Doublets produced spurious Slingshot branches on simulated data, and doublet removal most improved temporally DE genes when Slingshot was used (Xi and Li 2021, PMID 33338399)

name: scVelo
summary: Python RNA velocity toolkit with steady-state, stochastic and likelihood-based dynamical models of splicing kinetics, plus latent time and velocity graphs; the scverse default for velocity
gain: Wu 2026: scVelo (stochastic) among five methods recommended for core performance and scalability, while scVelo (dynamical) ranked 14th, below veloVI (8th); Luo 2026: scVelo-sto among methods recommended for million-cell atlases and among those with highest agreement
caveats: Velocity estimates change with the spliced/unspliced quantification pipeline (Soneson 2021; Wu 2026 found only three of 22 methods robust to it); Bergen 2021 reviews its limitations and pitfalls
cite_title: Generalizing RNA velocity to transient cell states through dynamical modeling.
publication_title: Generalizing RNA velocity to transient cell states through dynamical modeling.
qc_links: alignment-quantification:Spliced and unspliced abundances from five quantification tools differed substantially and changed the velocities scVelo estimated (PMID 33428615)

name: Scrublet
summary: Simulates doublets from the data and scores each barcode with a nearest-neighbour classifier, without needing clusters; the default doublet step in scanpy and many Python pipelines
recovers: singlets that a high-UMI cap would discard; cleaner clusters
gain: Ttoouli 2025 (hashing truth): most accurate tool by AUROC; Demuxafy 2024: with scDblFinder, classified the most doublets correctly in pools of 16 donors or fewer; Xi & Li 2021: strong in simulations and one of two methods whose HVGs beat the negative control at all doublet rates
caveats: Threshold is set between two modes of the simulated score distribution, which are often not bimodal; among the detectors most affected by simulated ambient RNA (Demuxafy 2024); still missed most hashing multiplets (Ttoouli 2025).
cite_title: Scrublet: Computational Identification of Cell Doublets in Single-Cell Transcriptomic Data
publication_title: Scrublet: Computational Identification of Cell Doublets in Single-Cell Transcriptomic Data

name: scvi-tools (scVI, scANVI)
summary: Variational autoencoders on raw counts with batch as a covariate (scVI), and a semi-supervised variant that uses cell labels (scANVI), giving a batch-corrected latent space and label transfer
gain: scIB: scANVI, Scanorama, scVI and scGen performed best overall, especially on complex atlas tasks
caveats: Primary paper is scVI (Lopez 2018) and scANVI (Xu 2021) is listed in papers, both independent of scIB. scIB shares an author (F. J. Theis) with the scvi-tools library paper (Gayoso 2022), not with the scVI paper it evaluated; Zappia 2025 shares him too. totalVI, from the same library, has its own record [[totalvi]]. Needs raw counts and benefits from a GPU.
cite_title: Deep generative modeling for single-cell transcriptomics.
publication_title: Deep generative modeling for single-cell transcriptomics.

name: MNN correction and fastMNN (batchelor)
summary: Corrects batches by pairing mutual nearest neighbour cells across batches and subtracting locally estimated batch vectors, in expression space (MNN) or PCA space (fastMNN)
gain: scIB: FastMNN embedding among the best four on the human immune task; MNN conserved cell-cycle variance well; not among the overall top methods in scIB or Tran 2020
caveats: Assumes at least one shared population between batches; MNN in full expression space is slow, which fastMNN addresses.
cite_title: Batch effects in single-cell RNA-sequencing data are corrected by matching mutual nearest neighbors.
publication_title: Batch effects in single-cell RNA-sequencing data are corrected by matching mutual nearest neighbors.

name: Luecken & Theis 2019 best-practice tutorial
summary: Tutorial and review that sets out a scRNA-seq workflow from QC to downstream analysis with recommendations drawn from independent comparison studies, applied to a public dataset
gain: recommended permissive, per-sample QC thresholds judged jointly on counts, genes and mito, and revisiting QC after clustering
caveats: Superseded for most steps by the 2023 scverse guide ([[heumos-2023]]); fixed example thresholds in the case study are often copied without the joint-inspection advice.
cite_title: Current best practices in single-cell RNA-seq analysis: a tutorial
publication_title: Current best practices in single-cell RNA-seq analysis: a tutorial

name: UMI-tools
summary: Barcode whitelisting, read tagging and network-based UMI deduplication that merges UMIs differing by sequencing errors, used inside many custom single-cell pipelines
recovers: accurate molecule counts where UMI errors would otherwise inflate counts
gain: network-based handling of UMI errors improved quantification accuracy on simulated data and on real iCLIP and scRNA-seq data, and improved scRNA-seq clustering (self-reported)
caveats: Slow on large droplet datasets compared with integrated pipelines; its whitelist step is a knee on read counts, not a cell caller; not in any independent single-cell workflow benchmark found.
cite_title: UMI-tools: modeling sequencing errors in Unique Molecular Identifiers to improve quantification accuracy
publication_title: UMI-tools: modeling sequencing errors in Unique Molecular Identifiers to improve quantification accuracy

name: MAD-based adaptive QC thresholds (scater/scuttle isOutlier, scanpy)
summary: Flags cells whose log counts, log genes, top-gene share or mito fraction lie several median absolute deviations from the median of their batch, instead of using fixed cut-offs
recovers: cells that fixed thresholds remove in samples or cell types with atypical baselines
gain: pipeComp: most clustering benefit is reached without stringent filtering; lenient rules (5 MADs, or 3 MADs on at least 2 metrics) limit loss of whole subpopulations
caveats: Computed on a mixed population it removes cell types with extreme but healthy values (pipeComp); thresholds computed per treatment follow the treatment. sc-best-practices uses 5 MADs plus mito > 3 MADs and > 8%. isOutlier and perCellQCMetrics now live in scuttle [[scuttle]]. Regressing out mito fraction or detected genes later is no substitute for QC, since in pipeComp it nearly always raised correlation with those covariates and lowered clustering accuracy.
cite_title: Scater: pre-processing, quality control, normalization and visualization of single-cell RNA-seq data in R
publication_title: Scater: pre-processing, quality control, normalization and visualization of single-cell RNA-seq data in R

name: scuttle (per-cell QC metrics, Bioconductor)
summary: Bioconductor package that computes per-cell and per-feature QC metrics (library size, detected genes, subset percentages such as mito) and flags outliers with MAD rules via perCellQCMetrics, isOutlier and quickPerCellQC
recovers: cells kept by batch-aware MAD thresholds instead of fixed cut-offs (see mad-adaptive-qc)
gain: none of its own; it is the implementation the OSCA book and many Bioconductor pipelines use for adaptive QC
caveats: Split out of scater in 2020 and has no paper of its own, so the scater paper is cited; outlier calls inherit the MAD caveats of [[mad-adaptive-qc]] (whole cell types with extreme healthy values can be removed if run on a mixed population without a batch or type block).
cite_title: Scater: pre-processing, quality control, normalization and visualization of single-cell RNA-seq data in R
publication_title: Scater: pre-processing, quality control, normalization and visualization of single-cell RNA-seq data in R

name: scATAC per-cell QC metrics (TSS enrichment, fragments, FRiP, nucleosome signal, blacklist fraction)
summary: Filters scATAC and multiome barcodes on unique fragment count, TSS enrichment, fraction of fragments in peaks, nucleosome signal and blacklist fraction, the ATAC equivalents of counts, complexity and mito fraction
recovers: cells whose low fragment counts are biology (small or quiescent nuclei) when TSS enrichment is still high
gain: none measured as cells retained; the metrics are the basis of ArchR, Signac, SnapATAC2 and Cell Ranger ARC QC
caveats: Thresholds are fixed by convention (ArchR default TSS enrichment >= 4 and >= 1,000 fragments) and vary by protocol, since TSS enrichment and FRiP differ systematically between scATAC methods ([[de-rop-2024]]); FRiP needs a peak set, which genome-bin pipelines do not build ([[chromap-qc]]).
cite_title: Single-cell chromatin state analysis with Signac
publication_title: Single-cell chromatin state analysis with Signac

name: Signac
summary: Seurat-compatible R toolkit for single-cell chromatin data that computes nucleosome signal, TSS enrichment, fragments in peaks and blacklist ratio for QC, then runs LSI, clustering and integration with RNA
recovers: none specific; standard QC entry point for 10x multiome in R
gain: scaled to over 700,000 cells (self-reported); Luo 2024: its LSI embedding was outperformed on clustering by SnapATAC, SnapATAC2 and aggregation, and correlated 0.5-0.75 with library size after removing the first component
caveats: QC thresholds are user-chosen from vignette defaults; depth leaks into LSI components beyond the first, so fragment-count differences between conditions can drive clusters.
cite_title: Single-cell chromatin state analysis with Signac
publication_title: Single-cell chromatin state analysis with Signac

name: Saelens et al. 2019: trajectory inference benchmark (dynverse)
summary: Benchmark of 45 trajectory inference methods on 110 real and 229 synthetic datasets for cellular ordering, topology, scalability and usability, with guidelines for choosing a method by dataset size and expected topology
gain: No method best for every topology; the method choice should depend mostly on dataset dimensions and trajectory topology. In the authors' results data (February 2019), Slingshot had the highest overall accuracy (0.706), then PAGA Tree (0.695) and SCORPIUS (0.672); in the 29-method preprint, Slingshot, TSCAN and Monocle DDRTree clearly outperformed the rest
caveats: Accuracy is scored against reference trajectories; QC choices were not varied. The published paper is paywalled: rankings are from the authors' results file (github dynverse/dynbenchmark_results, 08-summary/results.rds; the February and September 2019 versions agree on the top three by accuracy, but the September update puts SCORPIUS first on the combined score) and the preprint
cite_title: A comparison of single-cell trajectory inference methods.
publication_title: A comparison of single-cell trajectory inference methods.

name: SoupX
summary: Estimates a per-channel ambient (soup) profile from empty droplets and a contamination fraction from genes that should be absent, then subtracts the soup from each cell
recovers: specificity of marker and response genes in kept cells, so cells need not be dropped for ambient-driven mixed profiles
gain: Nie 2026: second-lowest error and smallest variance for absolute contamination across contamination levels; Cargnelli 2026: reduced mode (filtered matrix only) is one of three recommended methods and less prone than CellBender or DecontX to over-correct samples without ambient RNA; Schroeder 2026 (preprint): reliable removal with minimal count distortion
caveats: One contamination fraction per channel by design, so it underestimates and cannot capture cell-to-cell variation (Janssen 2023: Slc34a1 outside PT only 60% -> 54%); automated mode can miss strong contaminating genes (scCDC 2024). Running it before doublet detection lowered doublet recall (Meier 2026, preprint).
cite_title: SoupX removes ambient RNA contamination from droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing data
publication_title: SoupX removes ambient RNA contamination from droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing data

name: doubletCells / computeDoubletDensity (scran, scDblFinder)
summary: Scores each cell by the local density of simulated doublets relative to real cells in a reduced space; moved from scran's doubletCells to scDblFinder's computeDoubletDensity
gain: Xi & Li 2021: the only method that did not beat the library-size and gene-count baselines on a majority of the 16 datasets, and the only one that left spurious trajectory branches
caveats: Superseded by scDblFinder's classifier in the same package; retained in OSCA as a cluster-free score.
cite_title: A step-by-step workflow for low-level analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data with Bioconductor
publication_title: A step-by-step workflow for low-level analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data with Bioconductor

name: RCTD doublet mode applied to droplet doublets
summary: Proposes decomposing droplet doublets with RCTD doublet mode, which fits the best one or two reference cell types per Slide-seq pixel, to assign both partners and their mixing proportion
recovers: partner identities and proportions for doublets that would otherwise be discarded
caveats: untested on droplet doublets; in RCTD's own simulations transcriptionally similar pairs were called singlets 87.0% of the time; models platform effects, not ambient RNA or interaction-induced expression
cite_title: Robust decomposition of cell type mixtures in spatial transcriptomics
publication_title: Robust decomposition of cell type mixtures in spatial transcriptomics

name: Luecken et al. 2022, scIB atlas-level integration benchmark
summary: Benchmark of 16 integration methods in 68 method and preprocessing combinations on 13 atlas-level tasks (85 batches, over 1.2 million cells) with 14 metrics for batch removal and biological conservation
gain: scANVI, Scanorama, scVI and scGen best overall; HVG selection improved 74% of comparisons; scaling raised batch removal in 79% and lowered bio-conservation in 72%; cell-cycle and trajectory conservation favoured the full gene set
caveats: 40/60 weighting of batch removal against bio-conservation is a choice; label-based metrics depend on the annotation they are given.
cite_title: Benchmarking atlas-level data integration in single-cell genomics.
publication_title: Benchmarking atlas-level data integration in single-cell genomics.

name: SPLiT-seq / Parse Evercode
summary: Fixed cells or nuclei are barcoded in situ through rounds of split-pool ligation in plates, so the first-round well doubles as a sample barcode without hashing
recovers: samples per run (96-384 per commercial kit, vendor-reported) and storage of fixed cells; fewer stressed cells than unfixed droplet capture in one organoid comparison
gain: Independent: about 2x genes per cell against 10x 3' on mouse thymocytes (Filippov 2024); post-QC retention 95.6% against 87.2% and fewer stressed cells than 10x CellPlex on cerebellar organoids (Sarieva 2026); self-reported: 0.1% mouse-human collisions and about $0.01 per cell library preparation (2018)
caveats: Lower recovery from input: about 27% against 53% for 10x on PBMCs, 16.5% against 42.7% on organoids; about 80-85% of reads carry valid barcodes against 97-98% for 10x; collisions rise with cells per experiment (2.5% expected for 150,000 nuclei in the original 4-round design); vendor pipeline split-pipe is not open source
cite_title: Single-cell profiling of the developing mouse brain and spinal cord with split-pool barcoding
publication_title: Single-cell profiling of the developing mouse brain and spinal cord with split-pool barcoding

name: ArchR
summary: R suite for scATAC analysis whose arrow-file creation step computes per-cell TSS enrichment and fragment counts, applies QC thresholds, and scores doublets by projecting synthetic doublets, before clustering and integration
recovers: none specific; standard QC entry point for scATAC
gain: analysed over 1.2 million cells in 8 h on a laptop (self-reported); Luo 2024: with SnapATAC2 the most scalable of five feature-engineering methods, but its iterative LSI embedding stayed correlated 0.5-0.75 with library size
caveats: Default thresholds (TSS enrichment >= 4, >= 1,000 fragments) are protocol-dependent; its doublet scores are an RNA-free method distinct from AMULET; last code push February 2025. Doublet scoring is simulation-based and heterotypic only; on simulated PBMC multiplets recall was 0.25 and 0.23 against 0.80 and 0.90 for AMULET, though ArchR was higher (0.68 vs 0.37) on one low-depth islet sample (AMULET paper, a competitor comparison).
cite_title: ArchR is a scalable software package for integrative single-cell chromatin accessibility analysis
publication_title: ArchR is a scalable software package for integrative single-cell chromatin accessibility analysis

name: CellTypist
summary: Logistic regression classifiers trained on curated immune and tissue references that label each cell, with optional majority voting over over-clustered neighbourhoods
caveats: Labels are limited to the model's training types; no independent peer-reviewed benchmark including it was found. Paper is a cross-tissue immune atlas, so the human immune models are the best-supported ones.
cite_title: Cross-tissue immune cell analysis reveals tissue-specific features in humans.
publication_title: Cross-tissue immune cell analysis reveals tissue-specific features in humans.

name: Clustering and cell-type annotation
summary: Grouping cells into communities on a neighbour graph and naming them, by marker genes, by classifiers trained on references, or by mapping onto an annotated atlas
caveats: Cluster number depends on resolution and on every upstream step; automatic annotators lose accuracy for overlapping classes and deep annotation levels (Abdelaal 2019).
cite_title: Challenges in unsupervised clustering of single-cell RNA-seq data.
publication_title: Challenges in unsupervised clustering of single-cell RNA-seq data.

name: demuxlet / freemuxlet (popscle)
summary: Reference-genotype demultiplexer (popscle suite, with freemuxlet as its genotype-free mode) that scores each droplet's SNP reads against every donor and donor pair
recovers: donor labels and between-donor doublets from SNP reads
gain: Self-reported: in simulation 50 SNPs per cell assigned 97% of singlets and detected 92% of doublets in pools of up to 64; with genotypes for 8 pooled samples over 99% of singlets were assigned correctly
caveats: Default doublet threshold gave nearly 40% false-positive doublets in a synthetic test (souporcell authors); in pooled tumours only 31.9% of its doublet calls were true (Weber 2021); high memory use (Demuxafy); needs a VCF of the pooled donors
cite_title: Multiplexed droplet single-cell RNA-sequencing using natural genetic variation.
publication_title: Multiplexed droplet single-cell RNA-sequencing using natural genetic variation.

name: scLVM
summary: Latent variable model that estimates a cell-cycle covariance from annotated genes and removes it, exposing hidden subpopulations (successor f-scLVM handles many gene sets)
gain: revealed T helper 2 differentiation stages hidden by cell-cycle variation (self-reported)
caveats: Built for hundreds of cells; superseded and not maintained.
cite_title: Computational analysis of cell-to-cell heterogeneity in single-cell RNA-sequencing data reveals hidden subpopulations of cells
publication_title: Computational analysis of cell-to-cell heterogeneity in single-cell RNA-sequencing data reveals hidden subpopulations of cells

name: Tran et al. 2020, batch-effect correction benchmark
summary: Benchmark of 14 batch-correction methods on ten datasets in five scenarios (identical cell types across technologies, non-identical cell types, multiple batches, big data, simulated DE) with kBET, LISI, ASW and ARI
gain: Harmony, LIGER and Seurat 3 recommended; Harmony first because of its much shorter runtime
caveats: Simpler tasks than scIB; scVI was not among the methods tested.
cite_title: A benchmark of batch-effect correction methods for single-cell RNA sequencing data.
publication_title: A benchmark of batch-effect correction methods for single-cell RNA sequencing data.

name: scran pooled size factors (deconvolution)
summary: Sums counts over pools of similar cells to estimate pool size factors, then deconvolves them into per-cell size factors that are robust to many zero counts
gain: More accurate cell-specific size factors than library size or bulk methods on simulations (self-reported); pipeComp rated most normalisations, scran included, as fair
caveats: Pools are formed within quickCluster groups by default, so cells are pooled with similar cells; the default in the Bioconductor OSCA workflow. Applying QC filters within quickCluster groups in pipeComp removed almost no cells, unlike global filters.
cite_title: Pooling across cells to normalize single-cell RNA sequencing data with many zero counts.
publication_title: Pooling across cells to normalize single-cell RNA sequencing data with many zero counts.

name: EmptyDrops (DropletUtils)
summary: Calls cells by testing each barcode's profile against the ambient RNA profile estimated from low-count barcodes, so small low-RNA cells that differ from the soup are kept
recovers: low-RNA cells and whole cell types that a total-UMI knee threshold discards
gain: retained a putative interneuron cluster in ~900 brain cells and putative monocytes in placenta that the Cell Ranger v2 knee discarded; FDR among retained barcodes controlled at 0.1% (self-reported, simulations and real data)
caveats: Cell Ranger >= 3 runs an EmptyDrops-like second step, but its candidate set is bounded (the STARsolo EmptyDrops_CR emulation hard-codes umiMin 500 and umiMinFracMedian 0.01 as Cell Ranger values), so very low-RNA barcodes are never tested; DropletUtils defaults to lower = 100. In high-ambient samples it keeps empty and damaged droplets that need post-filtering (DropletQC found 0.4-9.5% cell-free droplets among EmptyDrops calls). Its result depends on the quantifier; on zUMIs and kallisto bustools output for a ~3,000-cell mixture it called ~60,000 cells (You 2021). In snRNA-seq of adipose tissue 87.9% of its passing droplets were nuclear against 95.7% for DIEM, and it removed 1,038 and 782 nuclear droplets in two samples (DIEM paper, competitor); hashing-labelled AUROC 79.87% in the EmptyNN paper (competitor).
cite_title: EmptyDrops: distinguishing cells from empty droplets in droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing data
publication_title: EmptyDrops: distinguishing cells from empty droplets in droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing data

name: decoupler / decoupleR (PROGENy, DoRothEA footprints)
summary: Framework that scores pathway and transcription-factor activities from prior-knowledge footprint gene sets (PROGENy, DoRothEA/CollecTRI) with methods such as univariate and multivariate linear models, on cells or on pseudobulk contrast statistics
recovers: One activity per pathway or regulator, pooling evidence from many weakly changed genes into a test with fewer comparisons
gain: decoupleR benchmark: simple linear models and a consensus score best predicted perturbed regulators; Holland 2020: footprint gene sets worked on simulated and CRISPR scRNA-seq comparably to bulk and partly better than SCENIC/AUCell and metaVIPER; PROGENy AUROC fell from 0.724 to 0.636 as gene coverage dropped
caveats: Performance depends more on the gene sets than on the statistic. Footprints come from bulk perturbation data in other contexts. Run on replicate-level contrast statistics to keep inference honest; cell-level scores inherit pseudoreplication. Benchmarks are from the same lab.
cite_title: decoupleR: ensemble of computational methods to infer biological activities from omics data.
publication_title: decoupleR: ensemble of computational methods to infer biological activities from omics data.

name: van den Brink et al. 2017 dissociation-induced expression
summary: Showed that enzymatic dissociation at 37 C induces immediate-early and heat-shock genes in subpopulations of cells, which can then appear as a distinct state
gain: none (cautionary finding)
caveats: Muscle stem cells; a stress cluster is a technical state to model or score, not necessarily a set of cells to remove.
cite_title: Single-cell sequencing reveals dissociation-induced gene expression in tissue subpopulations
publication_title: Single-cell sequencing reveals dissociation-induced gene expression in tissue subpopulations

name: Cell Hashing (antibody hashtags)
summary: Oligo-tagged antibodies against ubiquitous surface proteins label each sample before pooling, so samples share one lane and cross-sample multiplets become identifiable
recovers: cells per lane through superloading, and doublets that RNA-only methods miss
gain: 8-donor PBMC pool superloaded for about 20,000 singlets: modelled unresolved multiplet rate 3.1%, against about 4,000 singlets at the same rate without hashing (described as about 400% more cells for the same cost); observed 14,002 singlets and 2,974 identifiable multiplets
caveats: Needs surface epitopes, so weaker on nuclei (antibody nuclei hashing OCA 0.51-0.65 against 0.84 for cholesterol oligos in Mylka 2022); same-sample doublets stay invisible; calling with [[htodemux]], [[multiseqdemux]] or other T1 tools
cite_title: Cell Hashing with barcoded antibodies enables multiplexing and doublet detection for single cell genomics
publication_title: Cell Hashing with barcoded antibodies enables multiplexing and doublet detection for single cell genomics

name: HTODemux (Seurat)
summary: Seurat function that CLR-normalises hashtag counts, clusters droplets with k-medoids, fits a negative binomial to each tag's lowest cluster and calls the tag positive above that background's 0.99 quantile
recovers: sample labels for hashed cells; flags cross-sample doublets and tagless negatives
gain: Lowering positive.quantile from 0.99 to 0.9 raised overall classification accuracy from 0.54 to 0.65 on antibody-hashed nuclei of four cell lines (Mylka 2022); mean F 0.892, 0.794 and 0.742 on three BAL batches against vireo genotype truth, with under 20% of genetic doublets called singlets (Howitt 2023)
caveats: The vignette's per-tag CLR ignores per-cell tag depth, which Sayed 2025 found costs negatives; recall fell to 52% in a 30-sample imbalanced simulation and it errored on low-cell PDX batches (both reported by deMULTIplex2 authors)
cite_title: Cell Hashing with barcoded antibodies enables multiplexing and doublet detection for single cell genomics.
publication_title: Cell Hashing with barcoded antibodies enables multiplexing and doublet detection for single cell genomics.

name: Heumos et al. 2023 scverse best practices across modalities
summary: Review and online book (sc-best-practices.org) that summarises independent benchmarks into recommended workflows for scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, CITE-seq, immune repertoire and spatial data
gain: QC defaults of 5 MADs on log counts, log genes and top-20-gene share, mito flagged only when > 3 MADs and > 8%; SoupX for ambient RNA; scDblFinder for doublets; for ATAC, TSS enrichment, fragment counts and nucleosome signal
caveats: Where no independent benchmark exists the guide contrasts popular tools rather than ranking them; QC thresholds are defaults, not tested on treated or stressed cells.
cite_title: Best practices for single-cell analysis across modalities
publication_title: Best practices for single-cell analysis across modalities

name: Pseudobulk differential expression
summary: Sum counts per replicate sample (culture, well or donor) and cell type, then test with bulk RNA-seq tools (edgeR, DESeq2, limma-voom) so the replicate, not the cell, is the unit of inference
recovers: Calibrated p-values and bulk-concordant DE calls, from samples of any cell count, using mature small-n statistics
gain: All six top-ranked of 14 DE methods by concordance with matched bulk RNA-seq (AUCC) were pseudobulk methods across 18 gold-standard datasets (Squair 2021); pseudobulk had the highest average AUROC and best F1 among 18 methods (Junttila 2022)
caveats: Needs genuine replicates; with one culture per condition there is no between-replicate variance to estimate. Sum vs mean aggregation is disputed (Junttila 2022 favour sum; Murphy & Skene 2022 favour mean but attribute it to a simulation normalisation flaw). Less sensitive than cell-level tests by design. Batch covariate modelling beats batch-corrected input (Nguyen 2023).
cite_title: Best practices for single-cell analysis across modalities.
publication_title: Best practices for single-cell analysis across modalities.
qc_links: ambient-rna:Ambient RNA levels are sample-specific, and uncorrected DE between patients and controls called ambient transcripts as cell-type disease genes, so correct ambient RNA per sample before aggregating ([[fastcar]], PMID 38030970)

name: Squair et al. 2021: confronting false discoveries
summary: Benchmark of 14 DE methods on 18 datasets with matched bulk RNA-seq showing that methods ignoring replicate-to-replicate variation are biased toward highly expressed genes and call hundreds of DE genes when there is no biological difference
gain: Single-cell methods called hundreds of DE genes between randomly assigned replicates with no perturbation; pseudobulk methods abolished these; random-cell pseudo-replicates brought the bias and the false DE genes back
caveats: GLMMs could not be run on full datasets for compute reasons; on 25-50 cell subsets they were accurate only for specific parameter combinations. Directly relevant to split-well designs: aggregating random groups of cells into pseudo-replicates shrank variance most for highly expressed genes (46 datasets) and lost performance.
cite_title: Confronting false discoveries in single-cell differential expression.
publication_title: Confronting false discoveries in single-cell differential expression.

name: OSCA, Orchestrating Single-Cell Analysis with Bioconductor
summary: Paper and online book describing the Bioconductor single-cell workflow, including per-batch MAD outlier QC with scuttle, EmptyDrops cell calling, doublet scoring and ADT-specific QC
gain: QC chapter flags 3-MAD outliers within batch and recommends checking discarded cells for lost cell types by comparing their average profile with kept cells
caveats: The book is updated continuously, so its defaults may differ from the 2020 paper.
cite_title: Orchestrating single-cell analysis with Bioconductor
publication_title: Orchestrating single-cell analysis with Bioconductor

name: Milo (miloR, pertpy)
summary: Differential abundance testing on partially overlapping k-nearest-neighbour neighbourhoods with a negative binomial GLM across replicates and a spatial FDR correction, so abundance shifts are found without predefined clusters
gain: Yi 2024 (6 DA methods, synthetic and real data): Milo and Meld were robust and ranked top 2, and Milo performed best across a range of batch-effect magnitudes with the fewest hyperparameters to tune
caveats: Neighbourhoods depend on the kNN graph and its integration, so batch correction choices feed into results; needs replicates per condition; miloDE (PMID 39026254) extends the idea to cluster-free DE
cite_title: Differential abundance testing on single-cell data using k-nearest neighbor graphs.
publication_title: Differential abundance testing on single-cell data using k-nearest neighbor graphs.

name: BBKNN
summary: Builds the neighbour graph by taking each cell's nearest neighbours separately within every batch, so clustering and UMAP run on a batch-balanced graph without changing expression
gain: Fast and graph-only; evaluated in Tran 2020 and scIB without being among the recommended or top-ranked methods
caveats: Corrects only the graph, so downstream steps that read expression or PCA still see the batch effect.
cite_title: BBKNN: fast batch alignment of single cell transcriptomes.
publication_title: BBKNN: fast batch alignment of single cell transcriptomes.

name: Scanorama
summary: Finds mutual nearest neighbours across all datasets at once in a reduced space and stitches them panorama-style, returning a corrected embedding and corrected expression
gain: scIB: among the four best methods overall; its corrected-expression output conserved cell-cycle variance and HVGs best together with ComBat and MNN
caveats: Also tested by Tran 2020, which did not place it among its three recommended methods.
cite_title: Efficient integration of heterogeneous single-cell transcriptomes using Scanorama.
publication_title: Efficient integration of heterogeneous single-cell transcriptomes using Scanorama.

name: CellBender remove-background
summary: Deep generative model of droplet counts that calls cell-containing droplets, learns the ambient profile and returns background-subtracted counts
recovers: marker specificity in kept cells and cells that would otherwise be dropped or mislabelled because of ambient signal
gain: Janssen 2023 (genotype-mixed mouse kidney): most precise per-cell noise estimate; Slc34a1 detected in ~60% of non-PT cells raw, 7% after CellBender (SoupX 54%, DecontX 2%); Cargnelli 2026: best overall trade-off of ambient removal and endogenous retention; Nie 2026: top decontamination efficacy, robust to cell number and depth; Schroeder 2026 (preprint, 6 tools, droplet and BD Rhapsody data): reliable removal with minimal count distortion; Meier 2026 (preprint): the only one of three ambient tools after which doublet detection was not worse than before correction
caveats: Over-corrects when there is little or no ambient RNA (Cargnelli 2026); GPU strongly preferred; clustering gains are small and fine structure can be distorted (Janssen 2023); not independently benchmarked as a cell caller; in the EmptyNN paper (competitor) it kept 1,686 droplets against ~6,000 for other callers on genotype-labelled data (AUROC 58.02%).
cite_title: Unsupervised removal of systematic background noise from droplet-based single-cell experiments using CellBender
publication_title: Unsupervised removal of systematic background noise from droplet-based single-cell experiments using CellBender

name: Unbalanced optimal transport to model drug-induced cell loss
summary: Proposes carrying the growth and death terms of unbalanced optimal transport, which Waddington-OT estimates from proliferation and apoptosis signatures, into control-to-treated drug-response maps so that cell loss is modelled instead of ignored
recovers: a response model in which killed cells count as part of the effect
caveats: untested for drug screens; growth and death priors from signatures are weak in short exposures; balanced maps such as CellOT move all control mass onto the treated survivors
cite_title: Optimal-Transport Analysis of Single-Cell Gene Expression Identifies Developmental Trajectories in Reprogramming
publication_title: Optimal-Transport Analysis of Single-Cell Gene Expression Identifies Developmental Trajectories in Reprogramming

name: CellRank
summary: Combines a cell-cell similarity graph with directional information (RNA velocity, pseudotime or other kernels) in a Markov chain to find initial, intermediate and terminal states and per-cell fate probabilities
gain: Self-reported: recovered reprogramming outcomes on lineage-traced data and predicted a dedifferentiation trajectory in lung regeneration that was confirmed experimentally; Luo 2026 evaluated it among 15 velocity methods with mixed agreement
caveats: Inherits errors from the velocity or pseudotime kernel it is given, so quantification and QC choices upstream of velocity carry through to fate probabilities
cite_title: CellRank for directed single-cell fate mapping.
publication_title: CellRank for directed single-cell fate mapping.

name: cellity
summary: Support vector machine trained on over 20 biological and technical features, with microscopy-annotated broken, empty and multiple-cell capture sites as labels, that classifies low-quality cells
recovers: none; removes broken and empty captures that count thresholds miss
gain: over 30% higher classification accuracy than traditional threshold methods on about 5,000 Fluidigm C1 cells (CD4+ T cells, BMDCs, mESCs); SVM specificity 20-30% higher than unsupervised alternatives
caveats: Trained on C1 plate data with imaging ground truth; transfer to droplet data is untested. Repository last updated 2016, though the package remains in Bioconductor (release 3.23).
cite_title: Classification of low quality cells from single-cell RNA-seq data
publication_title: Classification of low quality cells from single-cell RNA-seq data

name: Denisenko et al. 2020 dissociation and storage biases
summary: Compared cold and warm dissociation, fresh, cryopreserved and methanol-fixed cells, and three single-nucleus workflows on adult mouse kidney
gain: cold dissociation recovered 330 podocytes (2.78%) against 3 (0.03%) warm; warm dissociation induced stress genes; cryopreservation gave about 30% fewer high-quality cells; nuclei gave more genes (median 1,819 vs 981) but fewer immune cells (0.73% vs 6.03%)
caveats: One tissue (mouse kidney).
cite_title: Systematic assessment of tissue dissociation and storage biases in single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq workflows
publication_title: Systematic assessment of tissue dissociation and storage biases in single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq workflows

name: scDblFinder
summary: Classifies cells against artificial doublets generated from cluster pairs with gradient-boosted trees, using the expected doublet rate as a prior
recovers: singlets that a cruder doublet filter or a high-UMI cut-off would discard; cleaner clusters
gain: Xi & Li 2021 protocol extension: highest mean AUPRC and AUROC on 16 real datasets with annotated doublets; singletCode 2024 replicated it as best on those datasets
caveats: Targets heterotypic doublets (its vignette reports low performance on homotypic ones); on lineage-barcoded ground-truth singlets all detectors were weak (mean AUPRC 0.13-0.34) and scDblFinder lowest (singletCode 2024), so in single-line drug screens most doublets are homotypic and need tags or genotypes. Run per capture lane (vignette: doublets only arise within a capture). ATAC mode aggregates correlated peaks instead of selecting features; the authors compared it with AMULET on three snATAC datasets and offer a Fisher combination of the two (F1000 v2). Demuxafy 2024 found scDblFinder and Scrublet the detectors most affected by added ambient RNA. Call doublets before decontX or SoupX correction; ambient correction first lowered detection (Meier 2026, preprint).
cite_title: Doublet identification in single-cell sequencing data using scDblFinder
publication_title: Doublet identification in single-cell sequencing data using scDblFinder

name: Abdelaal et al. 2019, automatic cell identification benchmark
summary: Benchmark of 22 supervised cell-type classifiers on 27 datasets for intra-dataset and inter-dataset prediction, feature sensitivity, cell number and annotation depth
gain: General-purpose linear SVM best overall; most classifiers did well but lost accuracy with overlapping classes and deep annotation; with stratified downsampling to under 500 cells most classifiers kept high performance
caveats: Predates CellTypist and Azimuth; the SVM-with-rejection result shows that accuracy can be bought with unlabelled cells (28.9% unlabelled at full size).
cite_title: A comparison of automatic cell identification methods for single-cell RNA sequencing data.
publication_title: A comparison of automatic cell identification methods for single-cell RNA sequencing data.

name: DecontX (celda / decontX)
summary: Bayesian mixture model that splits each cell's counts into native and contaminating parts using cell clusters, optionally with the empty-droplet profile
recovers: cell-level native counts without discarding cells; works when only a filtered matrix exists
gain: Cargnelli 2026: the only method of seven that did not reduce cell-type recovery; Nie 2026: best preservation of per-cell contamination ranking (with scAR) and named most accurate contamination estimate in the abstract; Janssen 2023: Slc34a1 outside PT 60% -> 2%; Schroeder 2026 (preprint): with scCDC, the only tool usable on non-droplet platforms without a raw matrix
caveats: Default mode failed on one single-nucleus replicate (87% residual, Janssen 2023); under-corrects highly contaminating genes (scCDC 2024); over-corrects when no ambient is present in full mode (Cargnelli 2026); rank robustness falls with depth (Nie 2026). Correcting with decontX before doublet detection retained the largest share of doublets, because it removes proportionally more counts from doublets (Meier 2026, preprint).
cite_title: Decontamination of ambient RNA in single-cell RNA-seq with DecontX
publication_title: Decontamination of ambient RNA in single-cell RNA-seq with DecontX

name: Hicks et al. 2018 technical variability and confounded batches
summary: Reanalysed published scRNA-seq studies and showed that systematic technical variation, including batch confounded with biology, explains a substantial share of cell-to-cell variability and the proportion of zeros
gain: none (cautionary finding)
cite_title: Missing data and technical variability in single-cell RNA-sequencing experiments
publication_title: Missing data and technical variability in single-cell RNA-sequencing experiments

name: totalVI (scvi-tools)
summary: Deep generative model of CITE-seq RNA and protein counts that models protein background and batch effects explicitly, for joint embedding, integration of panels, imputation and differential expression
gain: Hu 2024 (14 prediction and 18 integration algorithms, 47 datasets): totalVI with scArches best overall for predicting protein abundance, and totalVI with UINMF best in horizontal and mosaic integration (abstract)
caveats: Background is modelled per cell rather than measured from empty droplets as dsb does; GPU preferred for large data. Part of the scvi-tools library [[scvi-tools]]; Hu 2024 ran totalVI 0.17.4 for prediction and 0.19.0 for integration (authors' repository QuKunLab/MultiomeBenchmarking)

name: voomWithQualityWeights (limma sample weights)
summary: limma models a variance factor per sample (or per group) and combines it with voom observation weights, so noisy samples such as pseudobulks from few cells are down-weighted instead of removed
recovers: Power from samples that would otherwise be discarded as low quality
gain: Down-weighting variable samples gave a more powerful analysis with fewer false discoveries than removing them or weighting equally, in simulations and RNA-seq data
caveats: Weights are estimated from residuals, so they need residual degrees of freedom; with 1-2 replicates per condition they are unstable. A sample that differs for biological reasons can be down-weighted. dreamlet's cell-count weights are an a priori alternative.
cite_title: Why weight? Modelling sample and observational level variability improves power in RNA-seq analyses.
publication_title: Why weight? Modelling sample and observational level variability improves power in RNA-seq analyses.

summary: Measuring and jointly analysing more than one molecular layer per cell, such as RNA with surface protein (CITE-seq) or with chromatin accessibility (multiome), each with its own background, depth and QC metrics
caveats: Each modality has its own noise model: antibody counts carry ambient and non-specific background, ATAC is sparse with a narrow dynamic range, so RNA-centred QC and doublet calling do not transfer directly

summary: Pseudoalignment of reads to a transcriptome (or nascent plus mature, 'nac', index) written to BUS files, with barcode correction, UMI collapsing and counting in bustools, wrapped by kb-python

caveats: Sensitive to cell-type composition differences between batches, which it reads as batch effect; one of the scIB integration metrics; slow on large data without subsampling.

name: souporcell
summary: Genotype-free demultiplexer that calls variants from the pooled reads, clusters cells by allele counts with an explicit ambient-RNA term, and flags cross-genotype doublets
recovers: donor or cell-line labels for every cell with enough variant reads, independent of tags; an ambient RNA estimate
gain: Independent (Demuxafy): with vireo, unaffected by simulated ambient RNA in pools of up to 16 donors, but performance drops above 32 donors. Self-reported: 6 612 of 6 622 singlets and 415 of 451 doublets correct in a synthetic mixture; a minority sample resolved down to 0.6% of cells

summary: Mapping cells from several samples, lanes, protocols or studies into a shared space so that technical batch differences are removed while cell identities and states are kept
caveats: Integration removes whatever is declared as batch, and over-correction removes biology; scIB found that scaling raised batch removal in 79% of comparisons while lowering bio-conservation in 72%.

publication_title: Computational principles and challenges in single-cell data integration.

summary: Single-cell mode built into the STAR aligner that does barcode and UMI correction, gene, intron-inclusive (GeneFull) and velocity counting, optional multi-gene read allocation and Cell Ranger-like cell filtering in one pass

summary: Adds actinomycin D, triptolide and anisomycin (or actinomycin D alone in Act-seq) during enzymatic digestion so ex vivo immediate-early and stress genes cannot be induced
gain: abolished the ex vivo activated microglia (exAM) cluster (Fos, Jun, Hspa1a, Dusp1, Ccl3, Ccl4) seen after inhibitor-free digestion; no differentially expressed genes between mechanical dissociation with and without inhibitors (self-reported)
caveats: The same signature appears in postmortem human snRNA-seq, where it cannot be prevented, and was induced in resected human brain by elevated temperature ex vivo; validated mainly in brain myeloid cells.

name: mashr (multivariate adaptive shrinkage)
summary: Fits data-driven covariance patterns of effects across many conditions and returns shrunken effect estimates and local false sign rates per condition
recovers: Effects in conditions that are underpowered alone but share effect patterns with related conditions (drugs of one class, doses of one drug)
gain: GTEx eQTLs in 44 tissues: 47% of 707,036 top-SNP effects significant at lfsr < 0.05 with mash vs 13% for condition-by-condition ash and 39% for mash-bmalite
caveats: Needs per-condition effects and standard errors that are themselves valid, ideally from replicate-level pseudobulk. Contrasts against one shared vehicle control have correlated errors; mashr handles this through a reference condition in mash_update_data (common-baseline vignette). No single-cell drug-screen benchmark found.

gain: a PCA-based approach and the custom pair-based predictor performed best of six classifiers on published data, given prior cell-cycle genes and rank-based normalisation (self-reported)

summary: Fits dose-response curves to the number of cells recovered per hashed condition to estimate drug toxicity alongside the transcriptome, as done in sci-Plex
recovers: a viability phenotype from cell counts that would otherwise only set DE power

name: vireo (with cellSNP-lite)
summary: Bayesian variational model that assigns cells to donors from allele counts (cellSNP-lite pileups) with full, partial or no reference genotypes and calls between-donor doublets
recovers: donor or cell-line labels independent of tags; doublets between genotypes
gain: Most accurate and fastest of vireo, souporcell, freemuxlet and scSplit on simulated snRNA-seq pools (Fu 2025); best single method without reference genotypes at 16 or more donors (Demuxafy); on pooled tumours, 99.0-99.9% singlet recall with bulk RNA-seq genotypes and 99.2% of its doublet calls true versus 31.9% for demuxlet (Weber 2021)
caveats: Precision falls with doublets (100%, 85.9%, 77.4% at 0, 20, 30% doublets in Weber 2021); clustering can stall in local optima above ~16 donors (Souporcell3 authors); variant-caller pairing matters (60% recall for one cellSNP setting in Fu 2025)

summary: Dissociates tissue with a protease purified from a psychrophilic microorganism at 6 C or colder, so transcription is largely stopped while cells are released
gain: large reduction of 37 C dissociation artefacts in 20,424 P1 mouse kidney cells (self-reported); O'Flanagan 2019 and Denisenko 2020 independently confirmed lower stress signatures with cold dissociation
caveats: Slower and less complete digestion for some tissues; Denisenko found cell-type recovery shifts in both directions.

summary: Exchange over whether generalized linear mixed models with a random effect per sample or pseudobulk give more power at controlled type 1 error in hierarchical single-cell data
gain: Murphy & Skene: at equal type 1 error, pseudobulk mean had sensitivity >0.9 while all other methods had <0.9 (hierarchicell simulation, 5-40 individuals, 50-500 cells); Zimmerman: pseudobulk conservative and underpowered vs GLMM/MAST_RE
caveats: Both sides used the same simulator. The reply notes MCC can reward tests whose type 1 error exceeds 0.50. All agree cell-level tests without a sample term inflate type 1 error, and ComBat on the sample variable makes it worse. Lee 2024 proved count pseudobulk with a proper offset has the same point estimates and standard errors as a GLMM, more than 10x faster.

name: CPA and chemCPA (compositional perturbation autoencoder)

In the independent Ahlmann-Eltze 2025 benchmark CPA was particularly uncompetitive on double genetic perturbations (outside its design target). Predictions are not tests and carry no replicate-level uncertainty. scGen (2019) is the earlier latent-arithmetic model from the same group.

summary: Two doublet scores and their combination: cxds scores unlikely co-expression of gene pairs on binarised counts, bcds trains gradient boosting against artificial doublets, hybrid averages them
recovers: fast doublet scoring for large datasets without clustering
gain: Demuxafy 2024: scds, scDblFinder and Scrublet the top doublet detectors by MCC and balanced accuracy; Xi & Li 2021: cxds fastest and most resource-efficient, hybrid one of only two methods to beat the library-size and gene-count baselines on all 16 datasets
caveats: cxds alone has medium accuracy and cxds, bcds and hybrid were unstable at removing spurious clusters (Xi & Li 2021); bcds found the most unique multiplets but had the lowest accuracy against hashing (Ttoouli 2025).

name: Cell-subsample pseudoreplicates (one culture per condition)
summary: Splitting one well's cells into random subsets and treating them as replicates measures within-well sampling noise, so the resulting p-values test whether two wells differ, not whether a drug effect would reproduce in another culture
caveats: Squair 2021: random-cell pseudo-replicates shrank variance most for highly expressed genes (46 datasets) and reintroduced false DE genes in null comparisons. Lazic 2018: only 22% of surveyed animal studies replicated the correct entity-intervention pair and 46% pseudoreplicated. Honest uses: effect sizes, rankings, and comparison with a well-to-well null built from replicate control wells.

name: PIC-seq
summary: Sequences physically interacting cells (PICs) sorted as cell pairs and models each PIC transcriptome as a mixture of two singlet profiles, giving the mixing factor and the genes expressed above or below the mixture expectation
recovers: interaction-specific transcription from cell pairs that QC would discard as doublets
gain: re-use on human kidney allograft CITE-seq (31,203 libraries): 3 of 6 doublet clusters called physically interacting; two analysed clusters at 4.7x and 9.5x the expected artefactual-doublet frequency, mixing-factor regression R2 0.84 and 0.85
caveats: designed for FACS-sorted pairs; on unsorted droplet data it needs an expected random-doublet frequency, which common heuristics underestimate; assumes two-cell PICs; singlet references must come from the same sample

summary: Bayesian hashing demultiplexer in scanpy (sc.external.pp.hashsolo) that models signal and noise tag counts and scores each droplet's top tags under negative, singlet and doublet hypotheses with user priors

summary: Embeds cells with a variational autoencoder and trains a classifier head to separate simulated doublets from observed cells; now maintained inside scvi-tools

publication_title: Benchmarking algorithms for pathway activity transformation of single-cell RNA-seq data.

name: Revelio
summary: Rotates the PCA space to the plane in which cycling cells trace a circle and orders cells in cell-cycle time, with five phase labels
gain: Guo & Chen 2024: no method consistently best; Revelio assigns every cell to one of its five phases
caveats: Assumes the data are dominated by cycling cells (built on immortalised lines).
cite_title: The transcriptome dynamics of single cells during the cell cycle
publication_title: The transcriptome dynamics of single cells during the cell cycle

name: ddqc (data-driven QC)
summary: Clusters cells after minimal filtering, then applies MAD thresholds on genes, UMIs, mito and ribo fractions within each cluster
recovers: cell types with high mito or low complexity (neutrophils, metabolically active parenchymal cells) that global cut-offs remove
gain: retained a median 95.4% of input cells vs 69.4% with a fixed <200 genes / >10% mito cut-off ('over a third more cells')
caveats: A cluster made mostly of damaged cells sets its own baseline and can survive; MitoChontrol's perturbation test found ddqc kept many mito-inflated cells and removed some unperturbed ones.
cite_title: Biology-inspired data-driven quality control for scientific discovery in single-cell transcriptomics
publication_title: Biology-inspired data-driven quality control for scientific discovery in single-cell transcriptomics

name: Gruffi
summary: Scores glycolysis and ER-stress pathway activity on granular neighbourhoods and removes the stressed subpopulation found in brain organoids but not in fetal tissue
gain: identified an organoid-specific stressed population across about 190,000 cells and six validation datasets; removal improved resemblance to in vivo data (self-reported)
caveats: Built for organoids, where the stress is culture-induced hypoxia rather than handling; removes cells.
cite_title: Gruffi: an algorithm for computational removal of stressed cells from brain organoid transcriptomic datasets
publication_title: Gruffi: an algorithm for computational removal of stressed cells from brain organoid transcriptomic datasets

name: GMM-Demux
summary: Command-line tool that fits a two-component Gaussian mixture to each CLR-normalised tag and models droplet formation to estimate multiplet rates and flag multiplet-induced (phony) clusters
recovers: singlet calls with confidence scores; an estimate of undetectable same-sample multiplets for planning
gain: Howitt 2023: mean F 0.905, 0.770, 0.720 (BAL) and 0.823 (cell lines), under 20% of genetic doublets called singlets, judged close to demuxmix and HTODemux. Self-reported: PBMC multiplet rate cut from 23.9% to 6.45%, then 3.29% after removing 9 phony clusters
caveats: Bimodality assumption: failed to recover many samples in a 30-sample imbalanced simulation and errored on low-cell PDX batches (deMULTIplex2 authors); over-assigned doublets on a high-background CMO dataset (CMDdemux authors)
cite_title: GMM-Demux: sample demultiplexing, multiplet detection, experiment planning, and novel cell-type verification in single cell sequencing.
publication_title: GMM-Demux: sample demultiplexing, multiplet detection, experiment planning, and novel cell-type verification in single cell sequencing.

name: pertpy
summary: scverse Python framework for single-cell perturbation experiments that bundles harmonized perturbation datasets, metadata annotation, perturbation distances and implementations of established methods (Mixscape, Milo, scCODA, Augur, scGen and others)
caveats: A framework of re-implementations; each method keeps its own assumptions and benchmark record
cite_title: Pertpy: an end-to-end framework for perturbation analysis.
publication_title: Pertpy: an end-to-end framework for perturbation analysis.

name: You et al. 2021 preprocessing workflow benchmark
summary: Benchmark of 10 end-to-end preprocessing workflows (Cell Ranger, Optimus, salmon alevin, alevin-fry, kallisto bustools, dropSeqPipe, scPipe, zUMIs, celseq2, scruff) on CEL-Seq2 and 10x cell-line and tissue mixtures with known labels
gain: preprocessing choice mattered less than later steps; almost all workflow and normalisation combinations clustered well; cells unique to a subset of workflows were < 5% of cells; kallisto bustools and alevin-fry were > 50x faster than dropSeqPipe at 600M reads
caveats: emptyDrops called ~60,000 cells on zUMIs and kallisto bustools output for a ~3,000-cell mixture, so Cell Ranger v2 filtering was used there; the authors develop scPipe, so its results are not independent; 2021 versions.
cite_title: Benchmarking UMI-based single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing workflows
publication_title: Benchmarking UMI-based single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing workflows

name: sccomp
summary: Bayesian sum-constrained Beta-binomial model for differential composition and differential variability that models the proportion mean-variability association and identifies and excludes outlier observations
recovers: composition and variability changes robust to outlier samples
caveats: self-reported improvement over existing methods; outlier exclusion could hide a genuine extreme response, such as a highly cytotoxic well
cite_title: sccomp: Robust differential composition and variability analysis for single-cell data
publication_title: sccomp: Robust differential composition and variability analysis for single-cell data
publication_venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
qc_links: qc-metrics-thresholds:condition-dependent QC loss appears as composition change or as an outlier sample

name: TN test (valid post-clustering differential analysis)
summary: Truncated-normal test for marker genes between clusters that conditions on the clustering, so that the separation the clustering forced does not produce artificially low p-values
gain: Showed that reusing the same cells for clustering and DE gives artificially low p-values and false discoveries, and corrected them
caveats: Research code (notebooks), not maintained since 2019; the double-dipping problem it names is the lasting contribution.
cite_title: Valid Post-clustering Differential Analysis for Single-Cell RNA-Seq.
publication_title: Valid Post-clustering Differential Analysis for Single-Cell RNA-Seq.

name: TRADE (transcriptome-wide analysis of differential expression)
summary: Models the distribution of true DE effects from pseudobulk effect estimates and standard errors to estimate each perturbation's transcriptome-wide impact, including effects too small for per-gene significance
recovers: A per-perturbation effect-size summary that remains estimable when few individual genes pass FDR
gain: FDR-significant genes explained only 13-36% of estimated transcriptome-wide impact across five Perturb-seq screens (K562 genome-wide 36%, Jurkat essential 13%); a typical perturbation affected about 45 genes, essential genes over 500
caveats: Inputs are DESeq2 pseudobulk estimates per batch (perturbed vs unperturbed within batch), so validity rests on those standard errors. Downward bias for very small effects at finite sample size. Developed on CRISPR screens.
cite_title: Transcriptome-wide analysis of differential expression in perturbation atlases.
publication_title: Transcriptome-wide analysis of differential expression in perturbation atlases.

name: dreamlet
summary: R/Bioconductor pseudobulk workflow fitting precision-weighted linear mixed models per cell cluster, with initial weights from a Poisson model in which more cells and reads per sample mean higher precision
recovers: Samples with few cells stay in the model at lower weight instead of being dropped; plates, pools and batches can enter as random effects
gain: Poisson-initialised weights improved performance over the unweighted model; dreamlet controlled the permuted-label false positive rate (target 5%) across sample sizes where muscat limma-voom and glmer/MAST GLMMs were inflated; 2.2M cells from 1,000 donors x 12 cell types pseudobulked in 10 min with 20 GB
caveats: processAssays defaults: min.cells = 5 per sample-cluster, min.samples = 4 per cluster, min.prop = 0.4. Weights model measurement precision, not between-culture biological variance, so one culture per condition is still unreplicated. Built for cohorts of hundreds of donors. No independent benchmark of dreamlet itself; its engine dream (DREAM) was recommended as the quality/runtime compromise for atlas-level data by Hafner 2025.
cite_title: Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet.
publication_title: Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet.

name: Janssen et al. 2023 background-noise study
summary: Genotype-mixed mouse kidney scRNA-seq and snRNA-seq used to measure background noise per cell and to benchmark CellBender, DecontX and SoupX
gain: background made up 3-35% of UMIs per cell, mostly ambient RNA; CellBender gave the most precise estimates and the largest marker-gene improvement; clustering was fairly robust to noise
caveats: One tissue (kidney) and three methods; nuclei and cells differ in which method wins.
cite_title: The effect of background noise and its removal on the analysis of single-cell expression data
publication_title: The effect of background noise and its removal on the analysis of single-cell expression data

name: Soneson et al. 2021: preprocessing choices change RNA velocity
summary: Compared five quantification tools (13 approaches) for spliced and unspliced abundances in five droplet scRNA-seq datasets and showed that the differences propagate to estimated velocities and their biological interpretation
gain: Substantial between-tool differences in unspliced and spliced counts, concentrated in identifiable gene types, with large effects on velocity; both the feature definitions and the quantification algorithm matter
caveats: Shows sensitivity, not which pipeline is right; Wu 2026 later confirmed that most velocity methods are not robust to the quantifier
cite_title: Preprocessing choices affect RNA velocity results for droplet scRNA-seq data.
publication_title: Preprocessing choices affect RNA velocity results for droplet scRNA-seq data.
