name: scATAC-pro
summary: Workbench for scATAC-seq data from any protocol that computes QC metrics at each processing step, calls cells with a choice of methods and writes QC and analysis reports
recovers: a protocol-agnostic QC report for non-10x scATAC data
gain: none quantified
caveats: Last code push September 2024; cell-calling options have not been independently compared.
cite_title: scATAC-pro: a comprehensive workbench for single-cell chromatin accessibility sequencing data
publication_title: scATAC-pro: a comprehensive workbench for single-cell chromatin accessibility sequencing data

name: CellMixS (cell-specific mixing score)
summary: Cell-level batch mixing score (cms) that compares distance distributions to each batch within a cell's neighbourhood, separating local batch bias from unbalanced batch composition
gain: cell-specific metrics outperformed cell-type-level and global metrics on real and synthetic data (self-reported)
cite_title: CellMixS: quantifying and visualizing batch effects in single-cell RNA-seq data
publication_title: CellMixS: quantifying and visualizing batch effects in single-cell RNA-seq data

name: De Rop et al. 2024 scATAC-seq protocol benchmark
summary: Independent comparison of eight scATAC-seq methods in 47 experiments on reference PBMCs, processed with one pipeline (PUMATAC), measuring library complexity, TSS enrichment and fraction of fragments in peaks
gain: 169,000 PBMC profiles; methods differed in library complexity and tagmentation specificity, which carried through to cell-type annotation, genotype demultiplexing, peak calling, differential accessibility and motif enrichment
caveats: One sample type (PBMC); protocols and kits change quickly, so rankings age.
cite_title: Systematic benchmarking of single-cell ATAC-sequencing protocols
publication_title: Systematic benchmarking of single-cell ATAC-sequencing protocols

name: PhantomPurgeR (index-hopping model)
summary: Estimates the sample index-hopping rate in multiplexed droplet libraries and assigns each hopped read to its sample of origin, purging phantom molecules
gain: hopping probability 0.003-0.009, yet phantom molecules exceeded 8% in over 25% of samples and reached 85% in low-complexity samples; phantom molecules created phantom cells and turned empty droplets into apparent cells (self-reported)
caveats: Last repository update 2020.
cite_title: Model-based analysis of sample index hopping reveals its widespread artifacts in multiplexed single-cell RNA-sequencing
publication_title: Model-based analysis of sample index hopping reveals its widespread artifacts in multiplexed single-cell RNA-sequencing

name: MrVI (multi-resolution variational inference)
summary: Deep generative model in scvi-tools with a sample-aware latent space that computes counterfactual cells to stratify samples and find cell-state-specific DE and differential abundance without predefined clusters
recovers: Sample-level structure (which drugs or doses act alike) and local effects confined to cell subsets
gain: On sci-Plex A549 (92 drugs x 4 doses as samples), MrVI sample distances agreed better with Connectivity Map drug similarity and placed doses of the same drug closer together than PCA- or scVI-based stratification
caveats: Requires training a neural network on all cells. Counterfactual DE is model-based, not a replicate-level test. With one well per drug-dose the 'sample' is the well, so drug and well effects are confounded. No independent benchmark found.
cite_title: Deep generative modeling of sample-level heterogeneity in single-cell genomics.
publication_title: Deep generative modeling of sample-level heterogeneity in single-cell genomics.
qc_links: batch-and-plate-effects:Nuisance covariates such as plate are modelled apart from the target sample covariate, but only if plate is not confounded with drug

name: UDA-seq
summary: Overloaded droplets are barcoded first and a plate-based post-indexing round then splits each droplet barcode into single cells, across RNA, ATAC and multiome modalities
recovers: cells and samples per channel at a low collision rate
gain: Collision rate 1.23% with 96-well post-indexing against 6.29% expected from the droplet barcode alone; over 100,000 cells from three dozen frozen clinical biopsies in one channel
caveats: Cell recovery about 57% (3' RNA) and 37% (multiome); new method without independent benchmark
cite_title: UDA-seq: universal droplet microfluidics-based combinatorial indexing for massive-scale multimodal single-cell sequencing
publication_title: UDA-seq: universal droplet microfluidics-based combinatorial indexing for massive-scale multimodal single-cell sequencing

name: Buus et al. 2021 antibody titration for CITE-seq
summary: Titrates antibody concentration, staining volume and cell number for a 52-antibody 5' CITE-seq panel and shows that recommended concentrations cause unnecessary background from unbound antibody
recovers: protein signal and sequencing budget otherwise spent on background tags
gain: adjusted panel gave a 57% higher median positive signal and 43% lower background (median 26.3% to 14.9% of UMIs assigned to background); HLA-DR used 9% of cell-containing UMIs in lung tumour and could be cut at least fourfold
caveats: One panel and two samples (healthy PBMC, immune cells from a lung tumour); optimal titres depend on the antibody lot and the cell numbers stained.
cite_title: Improving oligo-conjugated antibody signal in multimodal single-cell analysis
publication_title: Improving oligo-conjugated antibody signal in multimodal single-cell analysis

name: Mylka et al. 2022 antibody versus lipid hashing comparison
summary: Comparison of antibody (TotalSeq-A, -B, -C), lipid (MULTI-seq, custom LMO, cholesterol CMO) and CellPlex hashing on cell lines, nuclei, PBMC and mouse tissues, scored against freemuxlet genotypes
recovers: tells which tag chemistry loses fewest cells for a sample type
gain: Overall classification accuracy 0.96 for antibody-hashed cell lines versus 0.68-0.84 for lipids (negatives 1.1-1.8% versus 7-21%); capturing 48% more cells raised doublets by 125% and unassigned barcodes by 325%; nuclei: cholesterol-oligo 0.84 versus antibody 0.51; brain cells: lipid 0.85-0.87 versus antibody 0.38; PBMC pre-sort labelling: TotalSeq-B 0.96, CellPlex 0.93
caveats: Cell-line results may not transfer to fragile or treated cells; dying high-mito PBMC clusters hashed worse; hashtag swapping ranged from ~0.1% (antibody) to 2.68% (custom LMO); one lab, four cell lines and few tissues; accuracy depends on the caller's parameters (HTODemux positive.quantile 0.99 to 0.9 raised antibody-nuclei OCA from 0.54 to 0.65); the freemuxlet reference itself misses some doublets
cite_title: Comparative analysis of antibody- and lipid-based multiplexing methods for single-cell RNA-seq.
publication_title: Comparative analysis of antibody- and lipid-based multiplexing methods for single-cell RNA-seq.

name: Cyclum
summary: Autoencoder with a circular latent variable that infers cell-cycle pseudotime and can remove the cell-cycle component
gain: more accurate and robust cell-cycle characterisation than existing approaches, and clearer subpopulations after removal (self-reported)
cite_title: Latent periodic process inference from single-cell RNA-seq data
publication_title: Latent periodic process inference from single-cell RNA-seq data

name: Du et al. 2020 STAR vs kallisto evaluation
summary: Third-party comparison of STAR (STARsolo for 10x) and kallisto (with bustools) on Drop-seq, Fluidigm and 10x data, including mouse cortex nuclei, for gene abundance, accuracy against RNA-FISH and resources
gain: STAR detected more genes with higher expression and agreed better with RNA-FISH Gini indices; similar or better cell-type annotation; kallisto ~4x faster with 7.7x less memory
caveats: 2019-era versions (kallisto 0.45-0.46, bustools 0.39.3); small datasets.
cite_title: Evaluation of STAR and Kallisto on Single Cell RNA-Seq Data Alignment
publication_title: Evaluation of STAR and Kallisto on Single Cell RNA-Seq Data Alignment

name: Optimised transcriptomic references for scRNA-seq (Pool et al. 2023)
summary: Rebuilds the gene annotation used for counting by extending poorly annotated 3' ends, adding a hybrid pre-mRNA mapping strategy and resolving overlapping genes, so reads lost as intergenic or ambiguous are counted
recovers: genes and marker genes missing from droplet data, and cell types they define
gain: recovered missing gene expression and revealed missing cell types and marker genes across mouse and human tissue datasets (self-reported, abstract)
caveats: Gains are specific to how badly the default annotation fits the tissue; requires re-running alignment; no independent comparison found. Related evidence that the annotation choice matters - Bruning 2022 found the unfiltered annotation (with pseudogenes) lowered mito fractions and gave up to 10% more cells per sample.
cite_title: Recovery of missing single-cell RNA-sequencing data with optimized transcriptomic references
publication_title: Recovery of missing single-cell RNA-sequencing data with optimized transcriptomic references

name: SinQC
summary: Flags technical-artefact cells whose gene expression pattern is inconsistent with their data-quality metrics (mapping rate, library size, detected genes), for plate-based full-length data
recovers: none; removes artefact cells
gain: applied to nine datasets; no retention numbers in the abstract
caveats: Built for early low-throughput plate data (2016); no public code repository found, only a lab web page.
cite_title: Quality control of single-cell RNA-seq by SinQC
publication_title: Quality control of single-cell RNA-seq by SinQC

name: Spike-in reference cells
summary: Adds standardised cross-species reference cells to every sample so that reads from the sample's genome inside reference cells measure that sample's contamination profile, which then drives decontamination of drug-treated islet cells
recovers: a per-sample ambient measurement and, in principle, an absolute denominator for cell counts
caveats: shown for decontamination in pancreatic islets (artemether, GABA, FoxO inhibitor, DMSO); use as an absolute cell-count reference in drug screens is untested
cite_title: Single-cell RNA-seq with spike-in cells enables accurate quantification of cell-specific drug effects in pancreatic islets
publication_title: Single-cell RNA-seq with spike-in cells enables accurate quantification of cell-specific drug effects in pancreatic islets

name: scVI differential expression (lvm-DE)
summary: Bayesian DE from scVI-family deep generative models: posterior log-fold-change estimates from the denoised model, with an empirical Bayes treatment of their uncertainty
recovers: Denoised, depth-corrected effect estimates for sparse genes
gain: Outperformed state-of-the-art methods at estimating log fold change and detecting DE genes between cell subpopulations
caveats: Compares groups of cells; sample-level replication is not modelled (MrVI adds that). The independent nested benchmark of Hafner 2025 found single-cell-specific methods including scVI no better than pseudobulk DESeq2 on individual datasets, and slower.
cite_title: An empirical Bayes method for differential expression analysis of single cells with deep generative models.
publication_title: An empirical Bayes method for differential expression analysis of single cells with deep generative models.
publication_venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

name: Differential expression and differential abundance between conditions
summary: Testing which genes change expression (differential state) or which cell populations change in abundance between conditions, with biological replicates as the unit of inference, usually by pseudobulk aggregation, mixed models or neighbourhood-level count models
caveats: Cell-level tests that ignore the replicate structure call hundreds of false DE genes (Squair 2021); every QC step changes which cells are summed into each replicate, so QC losses that differ by condition become DE or abundance results

publication_title: Differential Expression Analysis of Single-Cell RNA-Seq Data: Current Statistical Approaches and Outstanding Challenges.

name: Brüning et al. 2022 single-cell aligner comparison
summary: Independent comparison of Cell Ranger 6, STARsolo, kallisto, salmon alevin and alevin-fry on three 10x datasets (human PBMC, mouse heart after infarction, mouse endothelial atlas) for whitelisting, cells, genes, clustering and DE
gain: STARsolo, Cell Ranger 6, alevin and alevin-fry gave similar gene sets; kallisto reported the most cells but many were low-gene and unlabelled, and it detected extra Vmn and Olfr genes (likely artefacts); alevin found ~50% of cardiac endothelial cells; the unfiltered annotation gave up to 10% more cells per sample and lower mito fractions; STARsolo, alevin and kallisto were >= 3x faster than Cell Ranger 6
caveats: Three 10x datasets, default settings and 2021-era versions (kallisto before nac indices); no ground truth for cell identity beyond marker-based labels.
cite_title: Comparative analysis of common alignment tools for single-cell RNA sequencing
publication_title: Comparative analysis of common alignment tools for single-cell RNA sequencing

name: dropkick
summary: Trains a sparse logistic regression per sample on confident high- and low-quality barcodes from heuristic thresholds, then scores every barcode as cell or empty and low-quality
recovers: real cells below a knee cut-off in rare populations, while dropping dead and empty barcodes
gain: high-background simulations: specificity 0.9999 vs 0.9910 (Cell Ranger v2) and 0.9838 (EmptyDrops); colorectal inDrop data: more rare-population cells kept and more dead cells removed; AUROC 0.9817 agreement with EmptyDrops on 46 samples (self-reported)
caveats: Called > 9,000 barcodes on a 10x 8k PBMC sample where most callers called ~8,000 (valiDrops paper); no independent benchmark; last code push 2023-11.
cite_title: Automated quality control and cell identification of droplet-based single-cell data using dropkick
publication_title: Automated quality control and cell identification of droplet-based single-cell data using dropkick

name: MALAT1 as a cell-quality marker (Clarke & Bader 2024)
summary: Uses expression of MALAT1, a nuclear-retained non-coding RNA expressed in nearly all cell types, as a cheap proxy for the spliced/unspliced ratio to spot empty droplets and cytoplasm-poor cells
recovers: a damage signal without re-reading BAMs for spliced and unspliced counts
gain: MALAT1 expression was strongly correlated with the splice-ratio measure (preprint; no number in the abstract)
caveats: Preprint; applies only to species with a conserved MALAT1; single-nucleus data are nuclear by design, so a high MALAT1 there does not mark damage.
cite_title: MALAT1 expression indicates cell quality in single-cell RNA sequencing data
publication_title: MALAT1 expression indicates cell quality in single-cell RNA sequencing data

name: cellhashR (BFF_raw, BFF_cluster, consensus)
summary: R package that runs several hashing callers, including its own bimodal flexible fitting (BFF_raw, BFF_cluster), with tag QC plots and a consensus call across callers
recovers: singlets agreed by several callers, a hedge when no single caller is trusted
gain: Self-reported: BFF accurate and consistent on two reference datasets; no independent test of the consensus mode found
caveats: BFF assumes bimodal counts: in Howitt 2023 BFFcluster fell to mean F 0.119 and 0.188 on the weaker BAL batches, called no cells in one ovarian batch, and called over half (BAL) to over 75% (cell lines) of genetic doublets singlets; both BFF modes missed a whole sample in HTOreader's 8-donor pool. BFF also failed on hadge's brain nuclei and both modes ranked among the lowest workflows in Sayed 2025; its one independent win was BFF cluster on Brown 2024's low signal-to-noise CellPlex set, with four-fold more false positives on that study's high-quality MULTI-seq set. The consensus mode was not benchmarked
cite_title: BFF and cellhashR: analysis tools for accurate demultiplexing of cell hashing data.
publication_title: BFF and cellhashR: analysis tools for accurate demultiplexing of cell hashing data.

name: Weber et al. 2021 genetic demultiplexing in cancer
summary: In silico benchmark of genetic demultiplexing on pooled tumour scRNA-seq (high copy-number ovarian cancer, high mutation-burden lung adenocarcinoma) with a reusable Snakemake workflow
gain: cellSNP/vireo with bulk RNA-seq genotypes recalled 99.0-99.9% of singlets (precision 100%, 85.9%, 77.4% at 0, 20, 30% doublets); 1000 Genomes reference recall 97.9-99.0%; 99.2% of vireo doublet calls were true versus 31.9% for demuxlet
caveats: In silico pools; ambient RNA from debris lowered performance; souporcell, scSplit and freemuxlet not tested; scDblFinder performed poorly on the remaining doublets
cite_title: Genetic demultiplexing of pooled single-cell RNA-sequencing samples in cancer facilitates effective experimental design.
publication_title: Genetic demultiplexing of pooled single-cell RNA-sequencing samples in cancer facilitates effective experimental design.

name: SpotSweeper
summary: Spatially aware QC for spatial transcriptomics that compares each spot's metrics with its local neighbourhood to find local outliers and regional artefacts instead of using dataset-wide thresholds
recovers: spots in biologically low-count regions (for example white matter) that global thresholds remove
gain: identified a consistent set of systematically low-quality Visium barcoded spots across public datasets and two distinct regional artefact types (self-reported)
caveats: Neighbourhood size is a tuning choice; a Python port (Spotsweeper-py, 2025 preprint) exists.
cite_title: SpotSweeper: spatially aware quality control for spatial transcriptomics
publication_title: SpotSweeper: spatially aware quality control for spatial transcriptomics

name: deMULTIplex2
summary: R package that models tag cross-contamination from its physical mechanism with two negative binomial GLMs (tag-count and cosine-similarity spaces) fitted by EM, giving each cell a posterior sample probability
recovers: singlets from noisy, imbalanced or low-cell samples, including samples whose tag counts are not bimodal
gain: Self-reported: 63.2% versus 50.8% of all cells correctly retrieved (deMULTIplex) on multiplexed breast-cancer PDX, including two samples other callers missed; over 99% recall versus 52% (HTODemux) and 73% (demuxmix naive) in a 30-sample imbalanced simulation; accuracy held with about 10 cells per sample and with 5% of tag reads (median 30 tags per cell) on clean data
caveats: Tier rests on Sayed 2025: highest average F over 12 real datasets among the established standalone callers, behind only that study's own clustering workflows (F 0.87 versus 0.9 on its most depth-variable dataset). Competitor comparisons: tied best with CMDdemux on poorly hashed ovarian tumours (79% versus 81% concordance with vireo, CMDdemux paper), but failed on an over-labelled CellPlex PDX dataset (CMDdemux paper); cell-type bias in tag capture is reduced, not removed
cite_title: deMULTIplex2: robust sample demultiplexing for scRNA-seq.
publication_title: deMULTIplex2: robust sample demultiplexing for scRNA-seq.

name: GSFA (guided sparse factor analysis)
summary: Bayesian sparse factor model that infers co-regulated gene modules and each perturbation's effect on them, then propagates module effects back to individual genes
recovers: Gene-level perturbation effects detectable through shared modules when cells per perturbation are few (hundreds or fewer)
gain: In simulations GSFA calls at LFSR < 0.05 kept false discovery proportions well below 0.05 in most settings while edgeR-QLF and t-test calls were inflated in count-based scenarios, with higher power than t-test, edgeR-QLF and MAST
caveats: Cell-level model of CRISPR screens; well or culture replication is not modelled. Inference uses Gibbs sampling, which its authors note could be replaced by faster variational methods. No independent benchmark found.
cite_title: A new Bayesian factor analysis method improves detection of genes and biological processes affected by perturbations in single-cell CRISPR screening.
publication_title: A new Bayesian factor analysis method improves detection of genes and biological processes affected by perturbations in single-cell CRISPR screening.

name: Input-to-output recovery, split-pool versus droplet
summary: Independent comparisons that report cells recovered relative to cells put in for Parse split-pool barcoding and 10x droplet capture
gain: PBMCs (Xie 2024): about 53% of input cells recovered with 10x against about 27% with Parse, valid-barcode reads about 98% against 85%; cerebellar organoids (Sarieva 2026): 42.7% against 16.5%, with post-QC retention 87.2% against 95.6%
caveats: Two studies on different samples; Parse kits accept far more input cells, so a lower fraction can still give more cells; recovery depends on fixation and washing; De Simone 2025 reports recovery against target instead (Parse 122%), so denominators differ between studies
cite_title: Comparative Analysis of Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Methods with and without Sample Multiplexing
publication_title: Comparative Analysis of Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Methods with and without Sample Multiplexing

name: scAR (single-cell Ambient Remover)
summary: Variational autoencoder that learns the ambient profile from empty droplets and denoises RNA, protein, guide and ATAC counts
recovers: clean counts for RNA, CITE-seq and CRISPR guide assignments in kept cells
gain: Cargnelli 2026: highest ambient-removal score (0.679 vs CellBender 0.604); Nie 2026: most robust across conditions and, with CellBender, highest decontamination efficacy
caveats: Overestimates contamination (Nie 2026) and removed on average 0.445 of endogenous signal, mostly from low-expressed genes, hurting label transfer when no ambient was present (Cargnelli 2026); reassigned ~17% of cells to other types in one Nie 2026 dataset; preprint only. Created cell types absent from the raw data, 3 coarse types in BD Rhapsody and up to 8 in prefrontal cortex nuclei (Schroeder 2026, preprint).
cite_title: Probabilistic machine learning ensures accurate ambient denoising in droplet-based single-cell omics
publication_title: Probabilistic machine learning ensures accurate ambient denoising in droplet-based single-cell omics

name: De Simone et al. 2025 nine-kit comparison
summary: Nine commercial scRNA-seq kits run on PBMCs from one donor and scored on cost, time, cell recovery, read utilisation, sensitivity and cell-type resolution
gain: Cell recovery against target ranged from about 70% (BD Rhapsody) to 122% (Parse); 10x Flex top tier for genes per cell and best overall; Flex, 10x 3' and BD gave the highest UMIs per cell
caveats: One donor and PBMCs only; Parse and Scale were run once each because of kit cost; recovery uses each kit's own cell caller, and the Honeycomb and Fluent callers depend on user parameters
cite_title: A comprehensive analysis framework for evaluating commercial single-cell RNA sequencing technologies
publication_title: A comprehensive analysis framework for evaluating commercial single-cell RNA sequencing technologies

name: Mitochondrial filtering removes viable, drug-resistant malignant cells
summary: Shows across 9 tumour scRNA-seq datasets (441,445 cells, 134 patients) that malignant cells have higher mitochondrial fractions without more dissociation stress, and links high mitochondrial fraction to drug resistance in cell lines and resistant clones
recovers: viable high-mitochondrial malignant cells, including resistant clones, that a fixed 10-20% filter removes
gain: in 10-50% of tumour samples the malignant compartment had twice the high-mito share of the microenvironment, without higher dissociation-stress scores; across CCLE lines higher mito fraction associated with higher IC50 (drug resistance), median mito 4% (glioblastoma) to 14% (head and neck)
caveats: observational; drug link comes from bulk CCLE IC50 correlations and one ovarian line's lineage-traced clones, not single-cell drug screens; the 15% cut-off used to define high-mito is itself a convention
cite_title: Filtering cells with high mitochondrial content depletes viable metabolically altered malignant cell populations in cancer single-cell studies
publication_title: Filtering cells with high mitochondrial content depletes viable metabolically altered malignant cell populations in cancer single-cell studies

name: Montserrat-Ayuso & Esteve-Codina 2024 nuclear fraction in reference atlases
summary: Re-analysis of six reference atlases using intronic (nuclear) fraction and MALAT1 expression to find nuclei-free, low-quality cells left in after the atlases' own QC
gain: 6 atlases (Tabula Muris, Tabula Muris Senis, Tabula Sapiens, HCA liver and retina, a mouse kidney atlas), over 500 samples, 150 cell types and 20 tissues; some organs carry up to 85% low-quality cells
caveats: Argues for stricter filtering, the opposite direction to the salvage literature; the two agree that the deciding metric should be nuclear fraction, not mito or counts.
cite_title: High content of nuclei-free low-quality cells in reference single-cell atlases: a call for more stringent quality control using nuclear fraction
publication_title: High content of nuclei-free low-quality cells in reference single-cell atlases: a call for more stringent quality control using nuclear fraction

name: scDist
summary: Mixed-effects model of the distance between condition means in a low-dimensional expression space, with a random effect per sample, to rank which cell types or conditions changed while controlling individual and cohort variation
recovers: A replicate-aware answer to 'did anything change' when per-gene tests are underpowered
gain: Outperformed current methods in simulated and real datasets even with limited sample sizes, with fewer false positives from individual and cohort variation
caveats: Needs replicate samples. A cell-level permutation alternative, the E-test of scPerturb, permutes cells, so with one well per condition it tests whether two wells differ.
cite_title: Robust identification of perturbed cell types in single-cell RNA-seq data.
publication_title: Robust identification of perturbed cell types in single-cell RNA-seq data.

name: demuxmix
summary: Bioconductor package that fits negative binomial regression mixture models to raw tag counts, optionally with each droplet's detected-gene count as a covariate, and returns a posterior error probability for every assignment
recovers: weakly tagged singlets with normal RNA; supports pooling one untagged sample with tagged ones
gain: Best overall of 7 callers in Howitt 2023 (mean F 0.907, 0.833, 0.775 on BAL; under 20% of genetic doublets called singlets). Self-reported: 94% of singlets classified versus 87-93% for other callers (brain nuclei) and 85% versus 67-81% (cell-line mixture); untagged CSF cells pooled with tagged PBMC separated at sensitivity 0.980 and specificity 0.985
caveats: Weak on the poorly hashed ovarian tumour batches in Howitt 2023 (F 0.511 and 0.506) though with the fewest doublet errors; errored on all three low-cell PDX batches and reached 73% recall (naive mode) in a 30-sample imbalanced simulation (deMULTIplex2 authors); the RNA covariate gave no gain on Howitt's data
cite_title: demuxmix: demultiplexing oligonucleotide-barcoded single-cell RNA sequencing data with regression mixture models.
publication_title: demuxmix: demultiplexing oligonucleotide-barcoded single-cell RNA sequencing data with regression mixture models.

name: Arceneaux et al. 2023 contamination metrics and wet-lab fixes
summary: Contamination-based metrics computed before filtering (AmbientContaminationMetrics), tested in controlled experiments that vary dissociation, fixation, loading, dilution and cells vs nuclei
recovers: less ambient RNA at the source, so fewer cells need correction or removal
gain: metrics rose in proportion to spiked ambient level; cold protease, 0.1X DSP fixation, direct tip loading into the chip and ~1:1 dilution lowered contamination; 1% PFA failed QC; nuclei had universally higher contamination than cells
caveats: inDrop-centred experiments; dilution lowers cell recovery; the authors note many of these parameters are not adjustable on commercial platforms. Same lab as dropkick.
cite_title: A contamination focused approach for optimizing the single-cell RNA-seq experiment
publication_title: A contamination focused approach for optimizing the single-cell RNA-seq experiment

name: FastCAR
summary: Subtracts, per gene, the ambient counts expected from empty-droplet libraries below a chosen UMI cut-off, aimed at keeping ambient genes out of cell-type differential expression between conditions
recovers: condition comparisons not driven by sample-specific ambient RNA
gain: Nie 2026: with CellBender, closest to the measured baseline for absolute contamination (mtDNA genotype experiment); self-reported: in asthma bronchial biopsies ambient RNA levels were highly sample-specific and uncorrected DE called ambient transcripts as disease genes
caveats: Nie 2026: minimal per-cell correlation with true contamination and failed to remove MS4A1 from non-B cells; Cargnelli 2026: removes ambient mainly from highly expressed genes, eighth of nine in the overall ranking.
cite_title: FastCAR: fast correction for ambient RNA to facilitate differential gene expression analysis in single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets
publication_title: FastCAR: fast correction for ambient RNA to facilitate differential gene expression analysis in single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets

name: VeloCycle
summary: Bayesian RNA velocity model constrained to a periodic manifold that infers cell-cycle phase and speed with uncertainty
gain: cell-cycle periods validated against live imaging; detected speed differences between progenitors and after Perturb-seq knockdowns (self-reported)
caveats: Speed estimates are of interest in perturbation screens where drugs slow the cycle.
cite_title: Statistical inference with a manifold-constrained RNA velocity model uncovers cell cycle speed modulations
publication_title: Statistical inference with a manifold-constrained RNA velocity model uncovers cell cycle speed modulations

name: CyLinter
summary: Interactive QC tool for high-plex tissue imaging (CyCIF, CODEX and similar) that finds and removes cells affected by folds, debris, antibody aggregates, optical aberrations and segmentation errors
recovers: none; removes artefact-derived cells that otherwise form spurious clusters
gain: before cleaning, clustering of 25 TOPACIO specimens left ~29% of cells unclustered and many clusters traced to artefacts (self-reported)
caveats: Protein imaging rather than transcriptomics; relies on visual review at several steps.
cite_title: Quality control for single-cell analysis of high-plex tissue profiles using CyLinter
publication_title: Quality control for single-cell analysis of high-plex tissue profiles using CyLinter

name: Kuijpers et al. 2024 SPLiT-seq pipeline comparison
summary: Comparison of eight SPLiT-seq processing pipelines (alevin-fry splitp, LR-splitpipe, SCSit, splitpipe, splitpipeline, SPLiTseq-demultiplex, STARsolo, zUMIs) for speed, barcode calls and downstream results
gain: STARsolo, splitpipe and alevin-fry splitp handled large data in reasonable time; STARsolo was nearly identical to splitpipe; recommends splitpipe or STARsolo
caveats: One combinatorial chemistry; STARsolo needs extra code to collapse random-hexamer reads.
cite_title: Split Pool Ligation-based Single-cell Transcriptome sequencing (SPLiT-seq) data processing pipeline comparison
publication_title: Split Pool Ligation-based Single-cell Transcriptome sequencing (SPLiT-seq) data processing pipeline comparison

name: Minimum-cells rules for pseudobulk samples
summary: Per-sample cell-count floors applied before pseudobulk testing, for example muscat pbDS min_cells = 10 and dreamlet processAssays min.cells = 5 with min.samples = 4 per cluster
recovers: Lowering the floor and weighting by cell count keeps small wells as replicates instead of discarding them
gain: Matched scRNA-seq and bulk of the same cells: about 2,000 cells per cluster were needed to recover most DEGs with modest bulk differences, while 50-100 cells recovered most DEGs with extremely small bulk p-values or abundance above a few hundred TPM (Liu 2023)
caveats: The floors are software defaults, not values derived from a benchmark. Liu 2023 is a single-aliquot cell-level comparison, not a replicate-level test. Dropping a replicate costs a residual degree of freedom; whether a noisy kept sample at low weight beats dropping it is untested for drug screens.
cite_title: Robustness of single-cell RNA-seq for identifying differentially expressed genes.
publication_title: Robustness of single-cell RNA-seq for identifying differentially expressed genes.

name: CCPE
summary: Fits a discriminative helix to estimate cell-cycle pseudotime and phases and to remove cell-cycle effects
gain: competitive with existing methods on simulated and real data and robust to dropout (self-reported)
caveats: MATLAB implementation.
cite_title: CCPE: cell cycle pseudotime estimation for single cell RNA-seq data
publication_title: CCPE: cell cycle pseudotime estimation for single cell RNA-seq data

name: FixNCut
summary: Tissue is reversibly fixed with DSP before enzymatic dissociation, so dissociation-induced stress and necrosis are not written into the transcriptome
recovers: cells and states lost or distorted during dissociation and transport
gain: Preserved RNA integrity, library complexity and cell composition in human and mouse tissues while reducing stress-related signatures, on 10x 3' v3.1
caveats: Most relevant to tissues and organoids; cultured-cell screens can fix in the well instead; no independent benchmark yet
cite_title: FixNCut: single-cell genomics through reversible tissue fixation and dissociation
publication_title: FixNCut: single-cell genomics through reversible tissue fixation and dissociation

name: Rautenstrauch & Ohler 2026 silhouette shortcomings
summary: Showed that silhouette-based metrics (batch ASW, cell-type ASW) cannot reliably assess batch-effect removal or conservation of biological signal because their assumptions are violated in integration settings
gain: none (cautionary finding)
cite_title: Shortcomings of silhouette in single-cell integration benchmarking
publication_title: Shortcomings of silhouette in single-cell integration benchmarking

name: Howitt et al. 2023 hashtag demultiplexing benchmark
summary: Independent benchmark of 7 hashtag callers against vireo genotype assignments in 6 tagging experiments (24 BAL donors, 8 ovarian tumours, 3 lung cancer cell lines; antibody and lipid tags)
recovers: shows how many cells caller choice gains or loses when hashing is weak
gain: Genotype calls kept 81-91% of droplets as singlets, more than any hashtag caller; mean F ranged from 0 to 0.935 across callers and batches; demuxmix best overall, HTODemux and GMM-Demux close; hashing quality and RNA quality were largely uncorrelated
caveats: vireo is the truth, so genetic doublets and negatives are themselves imperfect; at most 8 tags per pool; deMULTIplex2 and demuxEM not included
cite_title: Benchmarking single-cell hashtag oligo demultiplexing methods.
publication_title: Benchmarking single-cell hashtag oligo demultiplexing methods.

name: Guo & Chen 2024 cell-cycle phase method comparison
summary: Compared Tricycle, Seurat CellCycleScoring, Revelio and CS1CC on four datasets with experimentally labelled phases (hESC and RPE1 FUCCI, mESC Quartz-Seq and Hoechst-sorted mESC) and on simulations
gain: no method consistently best; accuracy depends on the fit between reference or marker list and the data; Tricycle better on mouse than human; adding cells of known phase to the query improved all methods
caveats: Small, plate-based datasets (35-288 cells each) of cycling stem and epithelial cells; no droplet data, no drug-treated or non-cycling cells; cyclone not included.
cite_title: From G1 to M: a comparative study of methods for identifying cell cycle phases
publication_title: From G1 to M: a comparative study of methods for identifying cell cycle phases

name: Zappia et al. 2025, feature selection for integration and querying
summary: Benchmark of 24 feature selection methods and variants over ten datasets, scoring integration, query mapping, label transfer and detection of unseen populations with scVI, scANVI and Symphony
gain: About 2,000 features worked well; Seurat-VST (scanpy seurat_v3) highly variable genes ranked top; no consistent advantage for batch-aware scanpy variants; scANVI improved every metric category over scVI for the same features
caveats: From the scIB group, so not independent of scIB; 1,700 feature sets and over 6,000 integration runs; Symphony failed to detect unseen populations that scVI and scANVI separated.
cite_title: Feature selection methods affect the performance of scRNA-seq data integration and querying.
publication_title: Feature selection methods affect the performance of scRNA-seq data integration and querying.

name: sci-Plex-GxE
summary: sci-Plex extended with CROP-seq guide capture so drug, dose and CRISPR perturbation are read from the same nucleus, with two independent transductions per condition
recovers: true replicates (independent transductions) and hash-based doublet removal in a gene-by-drug grid
gain: 1,052,205 cells over 28,242 conditions (14,121 gene-by-environment combinations x 2 independent transductions); 94.3% of cells assigned to a condition after doublet removal; about 35 cells per condition on average (calculated from the reported totals); pilot: 94.4% of 18,585 cells assigned to a well
caveats: Few cells per gene-by-drug condition, so analyses pool guides per gene; guide assignment needed extra enrichment PCR cycles in complex libraries; no independent benchmark
cite_title: Multiplex single-cell chemical genomics reveals the kinase dependence of the response to targeted therapy
publication_title: Multiplex single-cell chemical genomics reveals the kinase dependence of the response to targeted therapy

name: ReDeconv and CLTS normalisation (transcriptome size)
summary: Normalises scRNA-seq by Count based on Linearized Transcriptome Size (CLTS), keeping the differences in total transcript content between cell types that per-cell scaling to 10,000 counts removes, and uses the result for bulk deconvolution
gain: Corrected DE genes that CP10K normalisation misidentified between cell types, with orthogonal validation, and improved deconvolution accuracy, notably for rare cell types
caveats: Gains are the authors' own. The point stands on its own: transcriptome size differs between cell types, often several-fold, so per-cell scaling before cross-type DE turns size into expression differences.
cite_title: Transcriptome size matters for single-cell RNA-seq normalization and bulk deconvolution.
publication_title: Transcriptome size matters for single-cell RNA-seq normalization and bulk deconvolution.

name: scRNABatchQC
summary: R package that compares many samples at once on technical and biological features (library size, mito, highly variable genes, pathway enrichment) in one HTML report to find outlier samples and batch effects
recovers: whole samples or lanes that would otherwise be judged one at a time and either kept with a defect or discarded
gain: none quantified
caveats: Diagnostic only, no filtering model; repository last updated 2021.
cite_title: scRNABatchQC: multi-samples quality control for single cell RNA-seq data
publication_title: scRNABatchQC: multi-samples quality control for single cell RNA-seq data

name: voomByGroup and voomQWB
summary: limma-voom variants for pseudobulk data whose groups have unequal variances: voomByGroup fits a separate mean-variance trend per group, voomQWB fits one quality weight per group
recovers: Power and error control lost when one high-variance group inflates (or a low-variance group deflates) the pooled variance
gain: Better error control and power than voom, voomWithQualityWeights and other gold-standard methods when group variances differ (simulations and several pseudobulk datasets); common BCV ranged 0.338-0.495 across groups in a lung macrophage dataset
caveats: Group-specific trends need several replicates per group; with 1-2 wells per drug they cannot be estimated, but they can separate a replicated control group from pooled treated groups. No independent benchmark found.
cite_title: Modeling group heteroscedasticity in single-cell RNA-seq pseudo-bulk data.
publication_title: Modeling group heteroscedasticity in single-cell RNA-seq pseudo-bulk data.

name: Neighbor-seq
summary: Classifies every barcode into singlet or multiplet types with a random forest trained on artificial multiplets, then tests each cell-type pair for enrichment against re-simulated multiplets to build a physical interaction network from routine scRNA-seq
recovers: cell-cell contact networks and neighbour-dependent expression from undissociated multiplets
gain: FACS-sorted DC-T doublets: sensitivity 52.1% (in vitro) and 29.2% (in vivo) at 98.9-99.2% precision, measured by the ULMnet authors
caveats: the null re-draws observed cells and does not model loading-dependent random doublet rates; cannot separate homotypic interactions from random homotypic doublets; lost to ULMnet in the only external comparison; default calls need >10 counts and P<0.05 per pair
cite_title: Reconstructing physical cell interaction networks from single-cell data using Neighbor-seq
publication_title: Reconstructing physical cell interaction networks from single-cell data using Neighbor-seq

name: CB2 (scCB2)
summary: Extends EmptyDrops by clustering similar barcodes before testing them against the ambient profile, which raises power for small cells
recovers: extra real cells, mostly in existing populations
gain: 24% more cells than EmptyDrops on average (range 4-81%), 88% of the extra cells joining existing subpopulations; +18% cells and a new 209-cell subpopulation in an Alzheimer snRNA-seq dataset
caveats: No independent benchmark; still needs post-filtering for damaged cells (valiDrops comparison, 2023).
cite_title: CB2 improves power of cell detection in droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing data
publication_title: CB2 improves power of cell detection in droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing data

name: Double-jeopardy (multi-omic doublet detection)
summary: Labels droplets with impossible receptor or protein combinations (several BCR/TCR chains, mutually exclusive CITE-seq markers) as doublets and trains a classifier on their transcriptomes to find further doublets, including homotypic ones
recovers: homotypic lymphocyte doublets that expression-only detectors miss
gain: high sensitivity and specificity in inflammatory-cell-dominant samples (self-reported, qualitative in the abstract)
caveats: Needs VDJ-seq or CITE-seq; anchored on immune cells.
cite_title: Double-jeopardy: scRNA-seq doublet/multiplet detection using multi-omic profiling
publication_title: Double-jeopardy: scRNA-seq doublet/multiplet detection using multi-omic profiling

name: scCDC
summary: Detects the genes that cause contamination and corrects only those, leaving lowly or non-contaminating genes untouched
recovers: housekeeping and lowly expressed genes that global correction removes
gain: self-reported: DecontX and CellBender under-correct highly contaminating genes and SoupX and scAR over-correct others, while scCDC corrects the former without the latter; Schroeder 2026 (preprint): with DecontX, the only tool usable on non-droplet platforms without a raw matrix
caveats: Independent benchmarks are lukewarm: moderate absolute error (RMSLE ~0.1), minimal per-cell correlation and failure to remove MS4A1 from non-B cells (Nie 2026); removes ambient mainly from highly expressed genes (Cargnelli 2026). Needs cluster labels.
cite_title: scCDC: a computational method for gene-specific contamination detection and correction in single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq data
publication_title: scCDC: a computational method for gene-specific contamination detection and correction in single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq data

name: ADTnorm
summary: Normalises antibody-derived tag counts by aligning the negative and positive peaks of each marker across samples and studies, with utilities for threshold gating and for scoring antibody staining quality
recovers: protein markers that batch-specific staining makes unusable across samples, and titration guidance from the staining-quality score
gain: against 14 scaling, normalisation and batch-correction methods (CLR, Arcsinh, logCPM, Harmony, fastMNN, CytofRUV, dsb, DecontPro, totalVI, sciPENN) on 13 public CITE-seq datasets, best alignment of positive and negative populations and cell-type separation
caveats: Comparison is the authors' own; peak detection needs a visible negative population, which some markers lack; manual peak adjustment is sometimes needed.
cite_title: ADTnorm: robust integration of single-cell protein measurement across CITE-seq datasets
publication_title: ADTnorm: robust integration of single-cell protein measurement across CITE-seq datasets

name: Demuxalot
summary: Reference-genotype demultiplexer that refines donor genotypes from the pooled reads before assigning cells, built for large pools
recovers: donor labels with the lowest error among genotype tools in Demuxafy
gain: Independent (Demuxafy): Demuxalot (refined) had the fewest wrong droplets, about 1% at 2 donors and 3% at 16 or more, and the best detection of between-donor doublets; combined with Dropulation it raised MCC by about 0.09 over single methods
caveats: Preprint only; needs reference genotypes; high memory use (Demuxafy)
cite_title: Demuxalot: scaled up genetic demultiplexing for single-cell sequencing
publication_title: Demuxalot: scaled up genetic demultiplexing for single-cell sequencing

name: hierarchicell
summary: Simulates hierarchical scRNA-seq data with within-sample correlation estimated from real data to estimate DE power by number of independent units and cells per unit
caveats: Its authors show that calculators counting cells instead of independent units grossly overestimate power. Murphy & Skene 2022 found the simulator omits a normalisation step that affects sum-pseudobulk results. powsimR (Vieth 2017) is an older simulation-based calculator.
cite_title: Hierarchicell: an R-package for estimating power for tests of differential expression with single-cell data.
publication_title: Hierarchicell: an R-package for estimating power for tests of differential expression with single-cell data.

name: Chord
summary: Ensemble that trains a gradient-boosting model on the scores of several doublet detectors (by default DoubletFinder, scds and others) against simulated doublets
gain: higher accuracy and stability than its component methods on real and synthetic data (self-reported)
caveats: Independent tests did not confirm the ensemble gain: Demuxafy (scds plus DoubletFinder intersection) outperformed Chord in pools of 8 or more donors, with Chord making more false singlet and false doublet calls; on singletCode barcoded data the ensembles (hybrid, Chord) did not always beat their components.
cite_title: Chord: an ensemble machine learning algorithm to identify doublets in single-cell RNA sequencing data
publication_title: Chord: an ensemble machine learning algorithm to identify doublets in single-cell RNA sequencing data

name: COMPOSITE
summary: Compound Poisson model that combines multiplet evidence from RNA, ATAC and protein in multiomic data
gain: on 17 trimodal DOGMA-seq datasets (280,123 droplets) with hashing truth it removed multiplet clusters that single-omic detectors left (self-reported)
cite_title: A unified model-based framework for doublet or multiplet detection in single-cell multiomics data
publication_title: A unified model-based framework for doublet or multiplet detection in single-cell multiomics data

name: SampleQC
summary: Fits a robust Gaussian mixture to per-cell QC metrics jointly across groups of samples with similar QC distributions, so each QC cell type gets its own component and outliers are called per component
recovers: rare cell types whose QC metrics differ from the dominant type, which single-population outlier rules remove
gain: in simulations the good cells wrongly excluded by miQC and scater-style MAD rules came almost entirely from one cell type, while SampleQC better preserved rare QC cell-type proportions; ran on 867k nuclei from 172 brain snRNA-seq samples
caveats: The authors note the simulation result depends on their design choices; the number of mixture components k is chosen per sample group by the user; QClus' own comparison on heart nuclei included SampleQC among seven alternatives it outperformed (self-reported by QClus). Repository last updated 2022.
cite_title: SampleQC: robust multivariate, multi-cell type, multi-sample quality control for single-cell data
publication_title: SampleQC: robust multivariate, multi-cell type, multi-sample quality control for single-cell data

name: singletCode (Zhang et al. 2024)
summary: Uses lineage-tracing DNA barcodes to extract ground-truth singlets and evaluate RNA-based doublet detectors on less heterogeneous data
gain: mean AUPRC 0.13-0.34 across DoubletFinder, scDblFinder, hybrid and Scrublet on barcoded datasets, with scDblFinder lowest there, although it was best on the original non-barcoded benchmark data
caveats: Barcoded datasets are mostly cell lines and lineage experiments, close to a single-line drug screen but with their own doublet structure.
cite_title: Synthetic DNA barcodes identify singlets in scRNA-seq datasets and evaluate doublet algorithms
publication_title: Synthetic DNA barcodes identify singlets in scRNA-seq datasets and evaluate doublet algorithms

name: Shainer & Stemmer 2021 kallisto vs Cell Ranger across organisms
summary: Reprocessing of 22 public 10x datasets from 8 organisms with kallisto and with Cell Ranger, comparing alignment rates, gene detection, cell numbers and clustering
gain: kallisto gave higher alignment and gene detection rates in most samples; Cell Ranger called more cells, but outside human and mouse the extra cells were low quality; kallisto processing of zebrafish pineal gland revealed an additional photoreceptor type
caveats: No ground truth; the cell-number difference reflects each pipeline's own cell calling as much as alignment.
cite_title: Choice of pre-processing pipeline influences clustering quality of scRNA-seq datasets
publication_title: Choice of pre-processing pipeline influences clustering quality of scRNA-seq datasets

name: EmptyNN
summary: Neural network trained by positive-unlabelled learning that separates cell-free from cell-containing droplets, using high-count barcodes as positives and the rest as unlabelled
recovers: cell clusters lost below a UMI cut-off, such as platelets
gain: hashing ground truth: AUROC 94.73% vs Cell Ranger v2 86.88%, v3 90.16%, EmptyDrops 79.87%, CellBender 88.80%; genotype ground truth: 96.30% vs 82.94-86.43% (CellBender 58.02%); recovered 885 barcodes below a 200-UMI cut, platelets with a median of 93.5 UMIs (self-reported)
caveats: Called > 9,000 barcodes on a 10x 8k PBMC sample where most callers called ~8,000, and needs post-filtering for low-quality cells (valiDrops paper); no independent benchmark; last code push 2024-01.
cite_title: EmptyNN: A neural network based on positive and unlabeled learning to remove cell-free droplets and recover lost cells in scRNA-seq data
publication_title: EmptyNN: A neural network based on positive and unlabeled learning to remove cell-free droplets and recover lost cells in scRNA-seq data

name: ccAFv2
summary: Neural-network classifier of six cell-cycle states plus a quiescent-like neural G0 state, with a confidence threshold that leaves uncertain cells unclassified
gain: better than or equal to other methods while calling more states (self-reported)
caveats: Preprint; G0, G1 and late G1 calls are less accurate outside neuroepithelial cell types.
cite_title: Classifying cell cycle states and a quiescent-like G0 state using single-cell transcriptomics
publication_title: Classifying cell cycle states and a quiescent-like G0 state using single-cell transcriptomics

name: cellCounts (Rsubread)
summary: Rsubread function that aligns 10x Chromium reads by seed-and-vote, collapses UMIs and assigns them to genes with featureCounts, all inside R
recovers: an R-native alternative to Cell Ranger for 10x data
gain: compared favourably with Cell Ranger and STARsolo on simulated and real data (self-reported)
caveats: No independent benchmark; 10x Chromium formats only.
cite_title: cellCounts: an R function for quantifying 10x Chromium single-cell RNA sequencing data
publication_title: cellCounts: an R function for quantifying 10x Chromium single-cell RNA sequencing data

name: GTE (group technical effects) per-gene batch metric
summary: Quantifies how much batch affects each gene, identifying a small set of highly batch-sensitive genes that dominate the batch effect
gain: as few as three highly batch-sensitive genes were enough to create a substantial batch effect; cell-level GTE outperformed existing batch quantification methods (self-reported)
caveats: Repository not checked.
cite_title: Quantifying batch effects for individual genes in single-cell data
publication_title: Quantifying batch effects for individual genes in single-cell data

name: HTOreader and hybrid hashing-genotype demultiplexing
summary: Hashing caller whose cut-offs resist many tags and unequal sample sizes, plus a hybrid strategy that names souporcell genotype clusters by their dominant hashtag and labels every cell that either method calls a singlet
recovers: hashing negatives and false hashing doublets in genetically distinct pools; one unhashed sample, or unstained aliquots of hashed donors
gain: Self-reported, 8-donor B and T cell pool: the hybrid added 5.2% singlets, mostly cells hashing had called doublets (715) or negatives (166); 88.03% of cells (13 777 of 15 650) assigned across a hashed and an unhashed pool sharing donors; about 100 hashtagged cells per donor sufficed to name clusters
caveats: Needs genetically distinct samples, so it cannot split conditions applied to one cell line; inherits souporcell's errors at high doublet rates
cite_title: A hybrid demultiplexing strategy that improves performance and robustness of cell hashing.
publication_title: A hybrid demultiplexing strategy that improves performance and robustness of cell hashing.

name: SkewC
summary: Flags cells whose gene-body read coverage is skewed relative to the protocol's typical profile, a QC signal independent of counts and mito fraction
recovers: none; removes cells that would otherwise form false clusters
gain: none quantified in the abstract
caveats: Most informative for full-length protocols (Smart-seq); 3' tag protocols have coverage piled at one end by design. Repository last updated 2023.
cite_title: SkewC: Identifying cells with skewed gene body coverage in single-cell RNA sequencing data
publication_title: SkewC: Identifying cells with skewed gene body coverage in single-cell RNA sequencing data

name: SoCube
summary: Deep-learning doublet detector that embeds gene expression into a 3D composite feature cube and classifies with an ensemble of multi-kernel CNNs
gain: better performance than existing detectors on benchmark datasets and downstream tasks (self-reported, no single headline number in the abstract)
cite_title: SoCube: an innovative end-to-end doublet detection algorithm for analyzing scRNA-seq data
publication_title: SoCube: an innovative end-to-end doublet detection algorithm for analyzing scRNA-seq data

name: CIcADA
summary: Calls heterotypic doublets as cells scoring above 0.75 for two cell types, clusters them with synthetic doublets of the same type pair and keeps only clusters made entirely of observed doublets as biological, then tests them for differential expression against the synthetic pairs
recovers: transcriptional programmes specific to juxtacrine contacts, from doublets
gain: FACS-sorted DC-T doublets: sensitivity 21.7% (in vitro) and 15.1% (in vivo), measured by the ULMnet authors
caveats: the synthetic-doublet contrast assumes random doublets equal the sum of two singlets; ambient RNA or shared state can push singlets over the two-score threshold; higher-order multiplets ignored (<3% of cells had >2 types above 0.75)
cite_title: Cell type-specific interaction analysis using doublets in scRNA-seq
publication_title: Cell type-specific interaction analysis using doublets in scRNA-seq

name: Counting intronic (nascent) reads, especially for nuclei
summary: Counting reads that fall in introns towards the gene (Cell Ranger include-introns, default from v7.0; STARsolo GeneFull; alevin-fry splici/USA mode; kb nac index) instead of discarding them
recovers: library size and genes in single-nucleus data, where much of the RNA is unspliced; cell types that exon-only counting blurs
gain: Kuo 2024 (independent, 10x mouse cortex nuclei): exon-only references gave significantly smaller library sizes and discordant SingleR labels for astrocytes vs neural stem cells; Pool 2023: intronic read handling is one of three causes of missing genes in droplet data
caveats: Adds a gene-length bias, plausibly from internal priming in introns (Kuo 2024); in whole-cell data intron counts lowered cross-workflow correlation without improving clustering (You 2021). Switching it on changes UMI totals, so cell calling and QC thresholds from older runs no longer apply. The split into spliced, unspliced and ambiguous differs between tools (DFK index vs splici and spliceu references).
cite_title: Quantification and statistical modeling of droplet-based single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data
publication_title: Quantification and statistical modeling of droplet-based single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data

name: valiDrops
summary: Filters barcodes with data-adaptive thresholds on standard QC metrics, keeps those whose clusters carry distinct marker signal, and flags dead cells with a trained classifier
recovers: a cell call that does not need post-filtering for low-quality barcodes, plus a dead-cell label that can be kept as a readout
gain: cell-type signals more distinct and consistent than after EmptyDrops, CB2, DIEM, dropkick, CellBender or EmptyNN filtering; dead-cell prediction median MCC >= 0.75 with as little as 0.1% dead cells (self-reported)
caveats: Dead-cell MCC fell to a median of ~0.66 in one dataset when half the true dead cells were removed; comparison is by its authors; no independent benchmark.
cite_title: Automatic quality control of single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq using valiDrops
publication_title: Automatic quality control of single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq using valiDrops

name: CLEANSER
summary: Mixture model, built on CRISPR barnyard assays, that gives the probability that each gRNA-cell assignment in a perturb-seq screen comes from the native rather than the ambient gRNA distribution, with gRNA- and cell-specific normalisation
recovers: correct guide assignments and the differential expression calls that depend on them
gain: self-reported: ambient gRNAs are a major source of false-positive guide assignments; the choice of ambient filter changed differential expression outcomes, and CLEANSER raised gRNA-cell assignment accuracy across CROP-seq and direct-capture formats against a strict UMI cut-off and the 10x mixture model
caveats: No independent benchmark; the authors note that gRNAs with greater coverage and larger UMI counts are assigned more accurately, and that hits found downstream still depend on the DE design.
cite_title: Characterization and bioinformatic filtering of ambient gRNAs in single-cell CRISPR screens using CLEANSER
publication_title: Characterization and bioinformatic filtering of ambient gRNAs in single-cell CRISPR screens using CLEANSER

name: DecontPro
summary: Bayesian hierarchical model that removes ambient and spongelet contamination from antibody-derived tag counts, after finding that some RNA-called empty droplets held high tag levels consistent with neutrophils
recovers: protein-defined cells hidden among RNA-called empty droplets, and cleaner protein signal
caveats: self-reported superiority; spongelets (medium-tag empty droplets) are a newly described artefact; recommends calling empty drops separately for RNA and tags
cite_title: Characterization and decontamination of background noise in droplet-based single-cell protein expression data with DecontPro
publication_title: Characterization and decontamination of background noise in droplet-based single-cell protein expression data with DecontPro

name: Arora et al. 2025 ambient mRNA and differential expression
summary: Shows on dengue PBMC and fetal liver data that uncorrected ambient transcripts enter cell-type DEGs and produce spurious pathways, and how CellBender and SoupX change this
gain: T cells: 17 significant GO terms before correction, all driven by immunoglobulin genes (13 found only before correction), 191 after CellBender and 46 after SoupX; Ig expression in T cells 0.54 -> 0.10 (CellBender) and 0.06 (SoupX)
caveats: Two correction tools, no ground truth; pathway counts depend on a rank-based DEG cut.
cite_title: Understanding and mitigating the impact of ambient mRNA contamination in single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis
publication_title: Understanding and mitigating the impact of ambient mRNA contamination in single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis

name: CellBouncer
summary: Toolkit for pooled experiments that demultiplexes by species, donor, mitochondrial haplotype, lipid tags or sgRNAs, and estimates per-cell ambient fraction and each source's contribution to the ambient pool
recovers: a per-donor or per-condition ambient profile in pooled lanes, and a doublet rate harmonised across data types
gain: outperformed existing methods at separating multi-species and multi-individual mixtures (self-reported, abstract)
caveats: New (2026); ambient estimation needs genetically distinct sources in the pool; no independent benchmark.
cite_title: CellBouncer, a unified toolkit for single-cell demultiplexing and ambient RNA analysis, reveals hominid mitochondrial incompatibilities
publication_title: CellBouncer, a unified toolkit for single-cell demultiplexing and ambient RNA analysis, reveals hominid mitochondrial incompatibilities

name: hadge (nf-core/hadge)
summary: Nextflow pipeline running 7 hashing and 5 genotype demultiplexers, scoring their agreement, with a rescue mode that labels genotype clusters by their matched hashtags
recovers: hashing negatives and whole weakly tagged samples when donors differ genetically
gain: Self-reported on hashed multiple sclerosis brain nuclei: rescue mode called 90% of droplets singlets and rescued 89.7% of hashing negatives, doubling singlets for the weakest hashtags; after the original study's QC, 3 208 cells were kept, 952 of them previously excluded
caveats: Two neuronal clusters were mostly or wholly rescued cells, so hashing loss was cell-type biased and rescue changes composition; needs genetically distinct donors
cite_title: hadge: a comprehensive pipeline for donor deconvolution in single-cell studies.
publication_title: hadge: a comprehensive pipeline for donor deconvolution in single-cell studies.

name: QClus
summary: Droplet filter for difficult single-nucleus samples that clusters nuclei on unspliced fraction, mito fraction and cell-type marker scores and removes empty and highly contaminated droplets
recovers: usable nuclei from high-ambient tissue (human heart) where count thresholds either keep contaminated droplets or remove too many nuclei
gain: against seven alternatives (Cell Ranger 7, CellBender, SampleQC, DIEM, DecontX, DropletQC, EmptyNN) on 6 datasets, 252 samples and over 1.9 million nuclei, highest quality in the most samples on all metrics and no processing failures
caveats: The comparison is the authors' own; default marker set and the initial filter (>= 500 genes, mito < 40%) are tuned for cardiac tissue and need changing elsewhere.
cite_title: QClus: a droplet filtering algorithm for enhanced snRNA-seq data quality in challenging samples
publication_title: QClus: a droplet filtering algorithm for enhanced snRNA-seq data quality in challenging samples

name: vaeda
summary: Combines a variational autoencoder with positive-unlabeled learning to give doublet scores and binary calls
gain: competitive with seven existing methods on the 16 Xi & Li benchmark datasets and ahead of the other Python-based methods (self-reported)
caveats: From the scds authors; not yet in an independent benchmark.
cite_title: Vaeda computationally annotates doublets in single-cell RNA sequencing data
publication_title: Vaeda computationally annotates doublets in single-cell RNA sequencing data

name: Ge et al. 2025, normalisation benchmark
summary: Benchmark of six normalisation methods (Seurat log, LIGER, Dino, SCnorm, sctransform, scran) on seven real and four simulated datasets, scored on clustering, DE and memory and run time
gain: Dino best for clustering 10x and large datasets; sctransform strong on full-length protocols; SCnorm suited to small datasets but averaged over 200 GB peak memory
caveats: Small benchmark; it describes the Seurat default as log10(x + 1), which is not what LogNormalize does, and counts LIGER (an integration method) as a normaliser. Weigh below Ahlmann-Eltze and Huber 2023.
cite_title: Single-cell RNA-seq data normalization: A benchmarking study.
publication_title: Single-cell RNA-seq data normalization: A benchmarking study.

name: scQCEA
summary: R package that writes an interactive QC report across sets of 10x samples and adds expression-based QC through cell-type enrichment against 2,348 marker genes for 95 human and mouse cell types
recovers: a check that a library carries recognisable cell types before it is judged on counts alone
gain: used 342 shallow-sequenced profiles to set minimum sequencing for its enrichment function; no retention numbers
caveats: Report and annotation tool rather than a filter; repository last updated 2023.
cite_title: scQCEA: a framework for annotation and quality control report of single-cell RNA-sequencing data
publication_title: scQCEA: a framework for annotation and quality control report of single-cell RNA-sequencing data

name: Cargnelli et al. 2026 ambient benchmark
summary: Independent benchmark of seven ambient RNA removal methods on simulated, species-mixing, genotype-mixing and contamination-free control data
gain: 7 datasets, 64 samples, 135,561 cells; 81.56% of cells carry some ambient RNA (mean 7.79% of UMIs in cells, 11.80% in nuclei); no single best method; recommends CellBender, DecontX (full mode) or SoupX (reduced mode)
caveats: Methods that remove most ambient (scAR, CellBender) also remove endogenous signal or over-correct clean samples; all methods but CellClear inflated marker fold changes beyond ground truth.
cite_title: Benchmarking computational decontamination of ambient RNA
publication_title: Benchmarking computational decontamination of ambient RNA

name: scIBD
summary: Self-supervised, iterative heterotypic doublet detector for single-cell chromatin accessibility data that adapts which simulated doublets it trusts
gain: outperformed other detectors on simulated and real scCAS datasets (self-reported)
cite_title: scIBD: a self-supervised iterative-optimizing model for boosting the detection of heterotypic doublets in single-cell chromatin accessibility data
publication_title: scIBD: a self-supervised iterative-optimizing model for boosting the detection of heterotypic doublets in single-cell chromatin accessibility data

name: SiftCell
summary: Identifies cell-containing droplets by comparing barcodes with randomised (shuffled) counterparts in manifold space (SiftCell-Shuffle), then models each barcode as a mixture of cell and ambient profiles (SiftCell-Mix)
recovers: a visual and statistical check on which barcodes are ambient-like, across droplet platforms
gain: described as more comprehensive and accurate than existing methods across several platforms (self-reported, abstract; no numbers in the abstract)
caveats: No independent benchmark; repository inactive since 2023-07.
cite_title: SiftCell: A robust framework to detect and isolate cell-containing droplets from single-cell RNA sequence reads
publication_title: SiftCell: A robust framework to detect and isolate cell-containing droplets from single-cell RNA sequence reads

name: Sayed et al. 2025 normalisation x caller benchmark (hashDemux)
summary: Benchmark of tag normalisations crossed with hashing callers on 12 real and simulated datasets, introducing hashDemux (per-cell CLR followed by clustering)
recovers: cells called negative only because their tag library was shallow
gain: Per-cell (sequencing-depth) CLR instead of per-tag CLR recovered ~97% (clustering) and ~56% (MULTI-seq workflow) of cells wrongly called negative for the most variable tag; best workflows F 0.9 versus 0.87 for deMULTIplex2 on that dataset; clustering with per-cell CLR had the highest average F over 12 datasets
caveats: At most 12 tags per dataset, mostly cell lines; the clustering workflow calls doublets poorly, so RNA-based doublet filtering is advised afterwards
cite_title: Systematic benchmark of single-cell hashtag demultiplexing approaches reveals robust performance of a clustering-based method.
publication_title: Systematic benchmark of single-cell hashtag demultiplexing approaches reveals robust performance of a clustering-based method.

name: Tahoe-100M
summary: Atlas of about 100 million cells from 50 cancer lines pooled as balanced cell villages in each well, treated with 1,100 drug-dose conditions and read with Parse split-pool barcoding plus SNP demultiplexing
recovers: cells per condition at atlas scale: each drug-dose well yields one condition per pooled line
gain: Preprint figures: 153 million barcoded cells, 95.6 million (about 62%) passed full filters; 52,886 line-drug-dose conditions with a median of 1,287 cells each; demuxlet benchmark accuracy above 98% with over 90% of cells called singlets; median correlation 0.975 for matched versus 0.915 for unmatched conditions
caveats: One well per drug-dose (plate 14 duplicated plate 6 and was held out for validation), so treatment is not replicated across wells; 3 of 50 lines dropped for consistently low counts; conditions under 50 cells excluded; control-media wells at fixed positions H11 and H12 of each plate, DMSO well count per plate not stated; design details read from the bioRxiv preprint
cite_title: Tahoe-100M: Mapping drug-induced molecular phenotypes at single-cell resolution
publication_title: Tahoe-100M: Mapping drug-induced molecular phenotypes at single-cell resolution

name: CellClear
summary: Estimates ambient expression programs by matrix factorisation using empty droplets and removes them from each cell
recovers: separation of closely related subtypes blurred by ambient RNA
gain: Nie 2026: top composite score at cell-subtype level; olfactory neurons with several receptor genes fell from 71 to 11; with scAR, most effective removal across tissues; Cargnelli 2026: the only method that did not inflate marker fold changes beyond ground truth
caveats: Schroeder 2026 (preprint): replaced > 93% of counts with factorisation-derived values and failed to scale to 172,000 nuclei; Cargnelli 2026: removed about as much endogenous RNA as ambient, mostly from lowly expressed genes; Nie 2026: overestimates contamination (RMSLE > 0.25) and missed 21 consensus B-cell markers. Preprint only.
cite_title: CellClear: Enhancing Single-cell RNA Data Quality via Biologically-Informed Ambient RNA Correction
publication_title: CellClear: Enhancing Single-cell RNA Data Quality via Biologically-Informed Ambient RNA Correction

name: Fu et al. 2025 genetic demultiplexing benchmark for snRNA-seq
summary: Benchmark of vireo, souporcell, freemuxlet and scSplit with three variant callers on simulated snRNA-seq pools of 2-6 samples at 0-30% doublets, checked against sex-linked genes
gain: All tools except scSplit reached 80-85% accuracy with high recall and precision; vireo was most accurate and fastest; scSplit recall was under 50%; accuracy fell as doublets rose
caveats: Simulated pools of few samples; results depend on the variant caller paired with each tool
cite_title: Benchmarking of computational demultiplexing methods for single-nucleus RNA sequencing data.
publication_title: Benchmarking of computational demultiplexing methods for single-nucleus RNA sequencing data.

name: Multi-round doublet removal (MRDR)
summary: Runs a doublet detector two or more times, removing calls between rounds, to offset the randomness of artificial-doublet simulation
gain: two rounds of DoubletFinder raised recall by 50% over one round on 14 real datasets; cxds twice was best on 29 barcoded and 106 synthetic datasets, with ROC up by at least 0.05 for all four tools tested (self-reported)
caveats: More rounds remove more barcodes, so the recall gain is partly a higher removal rate; singlet loss per round not reported in the abstract.
cite_title: Improving doublet cell removal efficiency through multiple algorithm runs
publication_title: Improving doublet cell removal efficiency through multiple algorithm runs

name: ambimux
summary: Read-level likelihood model that demultiplexes genotype-pooled RNA+ATAC multiome data while estimating each droplet's ambient fraction in each modality and classifying empty droplets
recovers: singlets at high ambient fractions that ambient-unaware demultiplexers lose
gain: simulations: ambient fraction MAE 0.048 (RNA) and 0.042 (ATAC); > 95% specificity with correct singlets up to 60% ambient, against ~25% for ambient-unaware models; 4,986 singlets from seven adipose biopsies in one channel (self-reported)
caveats: Preprint; needs donor genotypes; same group as DIEM.
cite_title: Integrated ambient modeling and genetic demultiplexing of single-cell RNA+ATAC multiome experiments with Ambimux
publication_title: Integrated ambient modeling and genetic demultiplexing of single-cell RNA+ATAC multiome experiments with Ambimux

name: demuxSNP
summary: Bioconductor package that trains a nearest-neighbour classifier (Jaccard distance on SNP profiles) on confident hashing singlets and simulated doublets, then reassigns negative, uncertain and doublet cells
recovers: hashing negatives and uncertain cells with good RNA when samples differ genetically
gain: Self-reported: beat hashing-only callers on a low-quality hashing benchmark and recovered more high-RNA-quality cells; in a renal cancer dataset HTODemux had left 2 582 cells (over 10%) negative; more robust than genotype-free and hybrid methods under class imbalance at 5-50% doublets
caveats: Needs genetically distinct samples and enough confident singlets per group; SNP coverage limits low-RNA cells
cite_title: demuxSNP: supervised demultiplexing single-cell RNA sequencing using cell hashing and SNPs.
publication_title: demuxSNP: supervised demultiplexing single-cell RNA sequencing using cell hashing and SNPs.

name: ImageDoubler
summary: Detects doublets and empty capture sites from the capture-chamber images of Fluidigm C1 runs instead of from expression
gain: detection rate up to 93.87% and at least 33.1% higher F1 than expression-based detectors (self-reported)
caveats: Needs the per-site images of image-capturing platforms (Fluidigm C1); not applicable to droplet data.
cite_title: ImageDoubler: image-based doublet identification in single-cell sequencing
publication_title: ImageDoubler: image-based doublet identification in single-cell sequencing

name: OmniDoublet
summary: Combines per-modality doublet scores from RNA and chromatin, weighting each by the Jaccard agreement of neighbourhoods across modalities, and thresholds the result with a Gaussian mixture
gain: superior accuracy, robustness and scalability against existing methods (self-reported, no number in the abstract)
cite_title: OmniDoublet: a method for doublet detection in multimodal single-cell sequencing data
publication_title: OmniDoublet: a method for doublet detection in multimodal single-cell sequencing data

name: RADO
summary: Doublet detector trained to maximise the area under the precision-recall curve on simulated doublets, for RNA and ATAC data
caveats: Preprint only (bioRxiv 2023); no PubMed record found.
cite_title: Robust and Accurate Doublet Detection of Single-Cell Sequencing Data via Maximizing Area Under Precision-Recall Curve
publication_title: Robust and Accurate Doublet Detection of Single-Cell Sequencing Data via Maximizing Area Under Precision-Recall Curve

name: RUVIII with pseudobulk pseudosamples (RUVIII-PBPS)
summary: Resample cells with replacement within biology-by-batch groups and pseudobulk them into artificial pseudosamples used only to estimate unwanted-variation factors for RUVIII when technical replicates or negative-control genes are missing
recovers: Removal of plate or processing effects from pseudobulk DE when only one single-cell sample per group exists to define replicates for RUV
gain: Processing-cohort ASW on 2 PCs fell from 0.17 to 0.06; FDR controlled where standard RUV could not be used; per-cell-type RUV2/RUVIII controlled FDR even under confounding
caveats: The pseudosamples feed factor estimation, not the DE test; the test still needs genuine replicates. Requires a known batch that crosses the biology of interest. Improper RUV on pseudobulk can remove biology.
cite_title: Removal of unwanted variation in pseudobulk analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing data and the leveraging of pseudoreplicates.
publication_title: Removal of unwanted variation in pseudobulk analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing data and the leveraging of pseudoreplicates.

name: Schroeder et al. 2026 ambient benchmark across platforms
summary: Preprint benchmark of CellBender, DecontX, SoupX, scCDC, scAR and CellClear on six human-mouse mixtures, PBMC, prefrontal cortex nuclei and a BD Rhapsody well-plate dataset, adding a count-integrity check
gain: CellBender and SoupX removed contamination reliably with minimal count distortion; CellClear replaced > 93% of counts; scAR created spurious cell types (3 coarse types in BD Rhapsody, up to 8 in cortex); DecontX and scCDC the only tools usable without a raw droplet matrix
caveats: Preprint (April 2026); species-mixing ground truth is partial (within-species ambient is invisible).
cite_title: Benchmarking ambient RNA removal across droplet and well-plate platforms reveals artificial count generation as a critical failure mode of scAR and CellClear
publication_title: Benchmarking ambient RNA removal across droplet and well-plate platforms reveals artificial count generation as a critical failure mode of scAR and CellClear

name: 10x Chromium Flex (fixed RNA profiling)
summary: Probe-based whole-transcriptome assay on formaldehyde-fixed cells or nuclei in which probe barcodes multiplex samples before droplet partitioning
recovers: fragile cells and queued samples through fixation and storage, and samples per run through probe barcodes
