gain: Independent: best overall of nine commercial kits on PBMCs and top tier for genes per cell (De Simone 2025); fixation retained fragile granulocytes better than fresh 10x 3' across nine sites after 4 weeks at -80 C (ABRF 2026); vendor-reported: up to 384 samples and 100 million cells per week in a 96-well plate format (October 2025 release)
caveats: Human and mouse probe sets only; probes miss most mitochondrial transcripts, so the mitochondrial fraction loses its usual QC meaning; more cross-site variation from on-site processing than other preserved workflows (ABRF 2026); core-facility guidance relaying 10x protocol CG000782: at least 25,000 (10x support advises 75,000) cells per fixation and over about 13,000 targeted cells per sample pushes multiplets above 5%

name: ABRF multisite preservation study 2026
summary: Nine core facilities processed the same fixed or cryopreserved leukocytes with 10x Flex, Parse Evercode WT v2 and Honeycomb HIVE and compared them with fresh 10x 3'
gain: After 4 weeks at -80 C, fixation (Flex) and cryopreservation (HIVE) retained granulocytes, about half of leukocytes, better than fresh 10x 3' processing; Flex showed more cross-site technical variation than the other preserved workflows
caveats: Comparisons are not symmetric (Flex against fresh 3', HIVE day 1 against day 28); leukocytes and PBMCs only; the Flex mitochondrial fraction is low by probe design
cite_title: Multisite Assessment of Methods for Cell Preservation Upstream of Single-Cell RNA Sequencing
publication_title: Multisite Assessment of Methods for Cell Preservation Upstream of Single-Cell RNA Sequencing

name: AmbiDose
summary: Combines an empty-droplet ambient profile with a per-cell removal budget and protects lineage-enriched genes, using the ambient dose to guide count removal rather than to estimate a calibrated contamination fraction
recovers: endogenous counts that global or overly aggressive correction removes
gain: held-out human-mouse GEM-X mixture: removed 92.0% of cross-species UMIs while retaining 99.6% of same-species UMIs; lowest proximal-tubule marker leakage across five strain-mixed kidney libraries (self-reported)
caveats: Preprint (September 2026); simulations showed reduced retention or incomplete removal when ambient and endogenous expression overlap; no independent benchmark.
cite_title: AmbiDose: per-cell removal budgets for ambient RNA contamination
publication_title: AmbiDose: per-cell removal budgets for ambient RNA contamination

name: AmbientMapper (scifi-demux)
summary: Maps reads competitively to several references, learns the ambient profile from empty and low-complexity barcodes and separates nuclei from background and singlets from doublets in combinatorial-indexing (scifi) data
recovers: low-depth nuclei discarded by read-count cell calling
gain: wrong-genome rate 0.19% on a 26-genome reference panel; calls robust across parameters and designs (self-reported, interspecies, multi-genotype and simulated read-level data)
caveats: Preprint; shown for scifi-ATAC (ambient chromatin) and needs multiple references or genotypes.
cite_title: Empirical Estimation of Ambient Contamination in Combinatorial Single-Cell Methods Using Multi-Reference Mapping
publication_title: Empirical Estimation of Ambient Contamination in Combinatorial Single-Cell Methods Using Multi-Reference Mapping

name: Boloori et al. 2026 gamma delta T cell counts vs QC choices
summary: Re-analysis of a public 3' snRNA-seq dataset of 33,600 small-intestine nuclei showing how calling strategy and QC stringency change the recovered fraction of one rare cell type
gain: gamma delta T fraction ranged 3.38-12.49% on the deposited matrix and 5.46-21.62% under strict filtering, a 3.70- to 4.08-fold spread; within one QC stratum the call rate rose from 0.51% to 12.17% across deciles of genes per nucleus
caveats: One dataset and one cell type; abstract-level numbers (no open full text found).
cite_title: How many gamma delta T cells are there? Calling strategy, quality control and receptor-locus specificity in 3-prime single-nucleus RNA sequencing of human small intestine
publication_title: How many gamma delta T cells are there? Calling strategy, quality control and receptor-locus specificity in 3-prime single-nucleus RNA sequencing of human small intestine

name: Chromap peak-free scATAC QC
summary: Extension of the Chromap aligner that reports peak-based QC metrics such as fraction of reads in peaks during alignment, without a separate peak-calling step
recovers: none; restores FRiP filtering to bin-based pipelines
gain: captured additional low-quality cells missed by SnapATAC2's QC and improved downstream results without extra compute (preprint, self-reported)
caveats: Preprint; no number of extra cells removed in the abstract.
cite_title: Quality control of single-cell ATAC-seq data without peak calling using Chromap
publication_title: Quality control of single-cell ATAC-seq data without peak calling using Chromap

name: ClusterDE
summary: Removes false-positive cluster markers caused by double dipping by repeating clustering and DE on a synthetic null dataset that matches the real gene means, variances and gene-gene rank correlations but holds one population
gain: Flags markers and clusters that over-clustering creates from one homogeneous population
caveats: Tests whether two clusters are distinct, not whether they are biologically meaningful; cite the published package paper rather than its preprint and Research Square versions.
cite_title: ClusterDE: A Statistical Software Package for Removing Double-Dipping Bias in Post-Clustering Differential Expression Analysis.
publication_title: ClusterDE: A Statistical Software Package for Removing Double-Dipping Bias in Post-Clustering Differential Expression Analysis.

name: CMDdemux
summary: Demultiplexer that CLR-normalises tags within each cell, clusters with K-medoids and classifies by Mahalanobis distance using hashtag and mRNA data, with plots for checking doubtful droplets
recovers: singlets on low-quality or over-labelled hashing data
gain: Self-reported: 81% concordance with vireo versus 79% for deMULTIplex2 on poorly hashed ovarian tumours, both ahead of other callers; on an over-labelled CellPlex PDX dataset recovered CMO301 singlets that HTODemux and demuxmix under-called while deMULTIplex2 and BFF failed
caveats: New (2026); no independent benchmark yet
cite_title: CMDdemux: an efficient single cell demultiplexing method.
publication_title: CMDdemux: an efficient single cell demultiplexing method.

name: Condition-aware QC audit (thresholds per cell type x batch, losses per condition)
summary: Set QC thresholds per cell type and batch (lane, plate), never per drug or dose, and tabulate cells removed by each QC step for every condition before any differential test
recovers: cells of treatments that shift mito fraction or RNA content and would otherwise be removed at a treatment-dependent rate
gain: none measured; drugs move the metrics QC relies on (paclitaxel and celecoxib repress global transcription per cell; mito fraction tracks drug resistance across CCLE lines)
caveats: Per-condition adaptive thresholds would normalise away a toxic drug's damage; a global fixed threshold removes cells at a rate the drug sets. Both bias pseudobulk comparisons; the loss table makes the bias visible.

name: Count cells per well, then balance input
summary: Record the number of cells or nuclei in each treated well before pooling, then pool similar numbers per well, so viability is kept as a phenotype while every condition gets comparable cell counts
recovers: cells per condition in cytotoxic wells, and the viability readout that equal-input pooling would otherwise erase
gain: No direct test; sci-Plex used hash-based nucleus counts per well as a viability measure, Tahoe-100M put roughly equal cell numbers per sample into barcoding, and scPerturb found that unequal cells per condition bias E-distance
caveats: Equal input cannot add cells to wells that died, so highly cytotoxic doses still need more seeding or pooled replicate wells; counting adds a step, and losses before counting may differ by treatment

name: CycleMix
summary: Gaussian mixture model over marker-gene scores that assigns any number of cell-cycle states and can call cells non-cycling
recovers: non-cycling cells that Seurat-style scoring forces into a phase
gain: better assignment and regression than Seurat and cyclone on six droplet datasets (self-reported)
cite_title: CycleMix: Gaussian mixture modeling of the cell cycle
publication_title: CycleMix: Gaussian mixture modeling of the cell cycle

name: CycleVI
summary: Deep generative model with a circular latent subspace that separates cell-cycle variation from the rest, giving a continuous phase and a residual space free of cell-cycle effects
recovers: signals entangled with proliferation, including drug responses, that score regression removes
gain: phase validated against protein-level measurements; preserved drug-response signals better than standard cell-cycle regression (self-reported)
cite_title: CycleVI: isolating cell cycle variation with an interpretable deep generative model
publication_title: CycleVI: isolating cell cycle variation with an interpretable deep generative model

name: Dostalova et al. 2026 dissociation workflow and reactive astrocytes
summary: A widely used commercial brain dissociation kit under-represented reactive astrocytes after ischaemic stroke compared with a low-shear workflow, selectively losing remodelling signatures
gain: none (cautionary finding); dissociation choice changed which disease-associated cells survived
caveats: One stroke model, with a preliminary similar trend in tauopathy.
cite_title: Tissue Dissociation Workflows Influence Reactive Astrocyte Recovery in Single-Cell Transcriptomics
publication_title: Tissue Dissociation Workflows Influence Reactive Astrocyte Recovery in Single-Cell Transcriptomics

name: DoubletDetection
summary: Repeatedly adds synthetic doublets, clusters with PhenoGraph or Louvain and scores cells by how often they fall in doublet-rich clusters, giving p-value based calls
recovers: singlets and cleaner clusters
gain: Demuxafy 2024: lowest share of wrongly classified droplets among doublet detectors (about 1% at 2 donors, about 3% at 16 or more); Xi & Li 2021: with DoubletFinder the most robust at restoring the correct number of clusters; Ttoouli 2025: among the top three by clustering quality
caveats: No peer-reviewed paper (cited by Zenodo DOI); failed on one of 16 datasets and among the slower methods (Xi & Li 2021).
cite_title: JonathanShor/DoubletDetection: doubletdetection v4.3.0.post1
publication_title: JonathanShor/DoubletDetection: doubletdetection v4.3.0.post1
citation_note: no citation count yet (run make enrich; or not indexed by OpenAlex)

name: Expected doublet rate from loading (Poisson / vendor table)
summary: Sets the number of barcodes a detector calls from the expected multiplet rate for the number of cells loaded, about 0.8% per 1,000 recovered cells on 10x Chromium
caveats: Ttoouli 2025 found the 10x rule consistently underestimates the multiplets marked by hashing; the rate covers all doublets, so in hashed or genotype-pooled data the within-sample (undetectable by tags) share is only about 1/N of it for N equal pools; Demuxafy ran Scrublet with R = N x 0.008 / 1000.

name: Expression-based label recovery for untagged cells
summary: Assigning hashing negatives to a sample with a classifier trained on confidently tagged cells' transcriptomes; sound when the label is a fixed identity (cell line, donor), circular when the label is the treatment whose effect is being measured
recovers: negatives and uncertain cells when no genotype difference separates the samples
gain: Identity labels only: MIX-Seq expression-based and SNP-based cell-line calls agreed over 99% (McFarland 2020); expression-aware demultiplexing reached mean accuracy 0.98 combined with genetics and added 1.4% on top of barcoding (Nassiri 2024). Treatment labels: no validated gain found
caveats: Cells assigned to a drug because they look treated inflate effect sizes and hide non-responders; keep such cells out of any comparison between the conditions the classifier separates, or use them only for condition-independent questions

name: hashedDrops (DropletUtils)
summary: DropletUtils function that removes ambient tag levels and calls singlets and doublets from the log-fold change between a droplet's top and second tag, with MAD-based outlier thresholds
recovers: more singlets when its confidence threshold is lowered
gain: With confident.min lowered from 2 to 0.5 it had the highest mean F in 4 of 6 batches in Howitt 2023 (BAL batch 2: 0.847 versus 0.613 at the default), at the cost of roughly doubling genetic doublets called singlets (about 3 000 extra in BAL batch 3)
caveats: Output hinges on hard thresholds and the default is too strict for weak hashing; on hashed brain nuclei it called 32 singlets out of 4 048 droplets (hadge 2024); no dedicated publication
cite_title: DropletUtils
publication_title: DropletUtils
citation_note: no citation count yet (run make enrich; or not indexed by OpenAlex)

name: Independent replicate wells or cultures per condition
summary: Each condition is applied to at least two independently seeded and treated wells or cultures, so the replicate unit for statistics is the well and not the cell
recovers: true replicates for pseudobulk testing and an estimate of well-to-well variance
gain: Cells within one sample are pseudoreplicates and treating them as independent inflates type 1 error (Zimmerman 2021, see also [[squair-2021]]); sci-Plex duplicate wells on randomised plates agreed at pseudobulk r = 0.99; sci-Plex-GxE used two independent transductions per condition
caveats: Doubles wells per condition; in pooled designs (MIX-Seq, Tahoe-100M) lines in one well share that well and are not replicates of the treatment; replicate plates confound plate with replicate unless layouts are randomised

name: Knee / inflection-point cell calling (barcodeRanks, Cell Ranger 2 style)
summary: Keeps barcodes above the knee or inflection of the ranked total-UMI curve, or above a fraction of a high quantile of expected cells; the default in STARsolo, kb and many alevin-fry runs
gain: none; simple and fast
caveats: Cannot tell a small or RNA-poor cell from an empty droplet, so low-RNA types are lost ([[emptydrops]]); in nuclei data a quantile threshold kept debris (only 84.5% of passing droplets nuclear vs 95.7% with DIEM, 6 adipose samples, PMID 32620816); the knee moves with intronic counting and depth, so the same sample processed two ways keeps different cells.

name: Martinez-de-Morentin et al. 2026 spatial segmentation benchmark
summary: Benchmark of 11 image-based, transcript-based and multimodal cell segmentation methods on 15 datasets from 5 imaging spatial transcriptomics technologies and 12 tissue types
gain: performance varied widely across datasets, technologies and metrics; segmentation choice changed cell-type specificity, transcript contamination between neighbouring cells and ligand-receptor inference
caveats: No single method wins; segmentation is the cell-calling step of imaging spatial data, so its errors look like doublets and ambient contamination downstream.
cite_title: Benchmarking segmentation methods for spatial transcriptomics
publication_title: Benchmarking segmentation methods for spatial transcriptomics

name: MitoChontrol
summary: Fits a Gaussian mixture to the mito fraction within each transcriptionally coherent cluster and sets a cluster-specific cut where the posterior probability of compromise exceeds a chosen level
recovers: viable cell populations with elevated mito fraction
gain: on HEK293 data with mtRNA inflated in 10% of cells it removed the inflated subset and kept the baseline; ddqc kept many inflated cells (qualitative, self-reported)
caveats: Preprint; no removal counts reported; depends on clustering; a global mito shift (all cells) is treated as biology, which is right for metabolic drugs but wrong if a whole condition is damaged.
cite_title: MitoChontrol: Adaptive mitochondrial filtering for robust single-cell RNA sequencing quality control
publication_title: MitoChontrol: Adaptive mitochondrial filtering for robust single-cell RNA sequencing quality control

name: MULTI-seq (lipid and cholesterol tags)
summary: Lipid- and cholesterol-modified oligos insert into membranes to barcode live cells or nuclei of any species before pooling
recovers: low-RNA cells that a UMI threshold would discard, and doublets including transcriptionally similar ones
gain: Independent (Mylka 2022): cholesterol-oligo hashing of nuclei reached overall classification accuracy 0.84 against 0.51-0.65 for antibody nuclei hashing, and lipids beat antibodies on mouse brain cells; self-reported: in a PDX tumour, 90.8% of sequenced neutrophils fell below the Cell Ranger UMI threshold and were kept by MULTI-seq classification
caveats: On cell lines lipid tags left more cells unassigned than antibodies (7% MULTI-seq LMO and 21% custom LMO against 1.1-1.8% TotalSeq) and swapped tags in 0.89% of singlets (Mylka 2022); BSA quenches LMO labelling of nuclei; calling with [[multiseqdemux]] or other T1 tools
cite_title: MULTI-seq: sample multiplexing for single-cell RNA sequencing using lipid-tagged indices
publication_title: MULTI-seq: sample multiplexing for single-cell RNA sequencing using lipid-tagged indices

name: Multiple TCR chains as a doublet marker in superloaded runs (Sserwadda 2025)
summary: In standard and superloaded multiplexed thymus and blood runs, over half of the T cells expressing multiple TCR chains were doublets, so receptor configuration adds a doublet filter that expression-based tools lack
gain: superloading caused minimal transcriptomic differences; over 50% of multi-TCR-chain T cells were doublets regardless of loading
caveats: Immune cells with paired VDJ data only.
cite_title: Superloaded Multiplexed scRNA-seq Data Preserves Primary Immune Cell Heterogeneity but Necessitates Stringent Doublet Removal
publication_title: Superloaded Multiplexed scRNA-seq Data Preserves Primary Immune Cell Heterogeneity but Necessitates Stringent Doublet Removal

name: MULTIseqDemux / deMULTIplex
summary: Classifier released with MULTI-seq (deMULTIplex R package, ported to Seurat as MULTIseqDemux) that sets each tag's threshold between kernel-density peaks by a quantile sweep that maximises singlets, iterating after removing negatives
recovers: sample labels for lipid- or antibody-tagged cells and nuclei
gain: Preferred caller in Mylka 2022 (freemuxlet truth): overall classification accuracy 0.96 on antibody-hashed cell lines and 0.84 versus 0.74 for HTODemux on cholesterol-oligo-hashed nuclei; with demuxEM, the closest match to vireo donors on hashed brain nuclei in hadge 2024
caveats: Assumes bimodal tag counts: deMULTIplex scored mean F 0.218 on a poorly hashed ovarian tumour batch (Howitt 2023) and missed whole PDX samples that its successor recovered (deMULTIplex2 authors); per-cell CLR before the sweep recovered ~56% of false negatives in Sayed 2025
cite_title: MULTI-seq: sample multiplexing for single-cell RNA sequencing using lipid-tagged indices.
publication_title: MULTI-seq: sample multiplexing for single-cell RNA sequencing using lipid-tagged indices.

name: Nie et al. 2026 ambient benchmark
summary: Benchmark of seven ambient RNA tools (DecontX, SoupX, scAR, CellBender, FastCAR, scCDC, CellClear) for estimation accuracy, robustness and subtype sensitivity on simulated and experimental data
gain: DecontX named most accurate contamination estimate (abstract); scAR most robust but overestimates; CellClear best for close subtypes; in the mtDNA-genotype experiment CellBender and FastCAR were closest to the empirical baseline (mean RMSLE < 0.06)
caveats: The abstract names DecontX most accurate for contamination level, while the mtDNA-genotype experiment in the results favours CellBender and FastCAR; robustness to fewer cells and lower depth differs by tool.
cite_title: Systematic benchmarking of ambient RNA decontamination tools to advance precision in single-cell transcriptomic analysis
publication_title: Systematic benchmarking of ambient RNA decontamination tools to advance precision in single-cell transcriptomic analysis

name: Optimus (HCA / WARP pipeline)
summary: Human Cell Atlas WDL pipeline for 10x data, STARsolo-based in current versions (multi-mappers allocated Uniform by default), that returns count matrices with emptyDrops results (lower bound 100 UMIs) and QC metrics attached rather than a pre-filtered matrix
recovers: an unfiltered matrix with per-barcode QC, so the user and not the pipeline decides which barcodes are cells
gain: You 2021: with kallisto|bustools, top 2 workflows on one downstream ranking (linear-model coefficients)
caveats: Assigned more counts to pseudogenes than Cell Ranger (You 2021, Optimus v1.3.6 and v2.0.0, older versions); fails when fewer than ~50 cells are called (WARP docs); designed for Terra/Cromwell execution; no dedicated paper.

name: Order of ambient correction and doublet detection (Meier et al. 2026)
summary: Preprint testing decontX, SoupX and CellBender before or after six doublet detectors on engineered and multiplexed data with known doublets
gain: doublet detection worked best before ambient correction, except with CellBender; decontX first retained the largest share of doublets; decontX and SoupX removed proportionally more ambient RNA from undetected doublets
caveats: Preprint (October 2026); conflicts with pipelines that correct ambient first.
cite_title: Order Matters: Ambient RNA correction confounds doublet detection in single-cell RNA sequencing
publication_title: Order Matters: Ambient RNA correction confounds doublet detection in single-cell RNA sequencing

name: Per-batch QC distributions and per-cluster batch composition
summary: Plots QC metrics by lane, plate or batch and tabulates each cluster's share of cells from each batch before integration, flagging clusters made of one batch and batches with shifted QC
caveats: A cluster from one batch can be real biology when batches differ in condition, which is why batch and condition must not be confounded by design.

name: Pooled residual variance for unreplicated drugs
summary: Fit one linear model across all wells so that drugs with a single well are tested against a residual variance estimated from replicated wells, such as several vehicle wells or a replicated subset of drugs
recovers: A replicate-level test for unreplicated drugs without inventing replicates from cell subsets
caveats: Assumes unreplicated drugs share the variance of the replicated wells; voomByGroup shows group variances often differ in pseudobulk data. Residual degrees of freedom come only from replicated conditions. Untested in single-cell drug screens.

name: QCatch
summary: Command-line tool that takes alevin-fry or simpleaf output, calls cells and writes an interactive HTML QC report (UMI distributions, sequencing saturation, splicing status) plus an annotated h5ad
recovers: none by itself; gives alevin-fry users the cell calling and QC report Cell Ranger users get by default
gain: none quantified
caveats: Tied to the alevin-fry ecosystem; its cell calling has not been benchmarked against EmptyDrops-style callers.
cite_title: QCatch: a framework for quality control assessment and analysis of single-cell sequencing data
publication_title: QCatch: a framework for quality control assessment and analysis of single-cell sequencing data

name: Regressing out cell-cycle scores (all phases or the S minus G2M difference)
summary: Removes cell-cycle variation by regressing gene expression on S and G2M scores, or only on their difference so that cycling and non-cycling cells stay separated
caveats: Removes any biology correlated with the scores, including proliferation changes that are a treatment effect; ccRemover and CycleVI authors report that score regression removes other signal (self-reported by competing methods); Massoni-Badosa note the same risk for any signature regression.

name: Scattered vehicle controls and randomised plate layout
summary: Vehicle (DMSO) wells are spread across rows, columns and edges of every plate and drug positions are randomised between replicate plates, so position and plate effects can be modelled instead of being confounded with treatment
recovers: unbiased within-plate controls and the ability to separate plate position from drug effect
gain: Bulk high-throughput screening, not single-cell: with active-drug plates above about 20% hit rate, normalisation using edge-placed controls failed while scattered controls plus Loess reduced row, column and edge effects (Mpindi 2015, simulated 384-well plates); not yet measured for single-cell transcriptomic readouts
caveats: Transfer from viability screens to scRNA-seq is assumed; sci-Plex randomised positions between replicate plates and Tahoe-100M placed control-media wells at fixed positions H11 and H12, and neither reported a position-effect analysis; how many DMSO wells per plate are enough is untested

name: Score cell cycle as a response readout, regress it only within condition
summary: In drug and genetic screens, phase shifts and arrest are part of the response, so phase fractions per condition should be reported and modelled, and any cell-cycle removal done within condition or by disentangling (CycleVI) rather than by global score regression
recovers: proliferation and arrest effects that global regression removes
gain: none measured for global regression in screens; CycleVI reports better preservation of drug-response signals than standard regression (self-reported); VeloCycle detected cycle-speed changes after Perturb-seq knockdowns
caveats: Phase calls themselves are uncertain (no method consistently best, Guo & Chen 2024), so condition differences in phase should be checked with a second caller.

name: scQCenrich
summary: Multi-metric post-cell-calling QC that adds intronic fraction, MALAT1 enrichment, dissociation-stress features and optional splicing to counts, genes and mito
recovers: neuronal, cardiomyocyte, erythroid and malignant cells that single-metric thresholds over-filter
gain: 10x mouse brain: removed 1,185 cells vs Seurat-style 2,520, scater 1,801, miQC 2,770, DropletQC 1,968
caveats: New (2026); comparisons are by its authors; whole-cell data only. For MALAT1 as a quality signal see [[malat1-quality-marker]] (preprint).
cite_title: ScQCenrich enables multi-metric quality control for single-cell RNA sequencing
publication_title: ScQCenrich enables multi-metric quality control for single-cell RNA sequencing

name: SEBULA
summary: Semi-parametric empirical Bayes multiplet caller for snATAC-seq that models the singlet background from fragments, gives FDR-controlled probabilities and can add evidence from paired RNA
gain: better sensitivity and specificity than snATAC-seq methods across simulations and seven multimodal datasets with hashing truth (self-reported)
caveats: No synthetic doublets, so no dependence on cluster structure; new (2026).
cite_title: Semi-parametric empirical bayes method for multiplet detection in snATAC-seq with probabilistic multi-omic integration
publication_title: Semi-parametric empirical bayes method for multiplet detection in snATAC-seq with probabilistic multi-omic integration

name: Separate handling stress from drug-induced stress with matched vehicle wells
summary: Many drugs induce the same immediate-early and heat-shock genes as dissociation, so a stress score should be compared with vehicle wells handled in the same lane and time, and only the vehicle-matched excess read as response
recovers: genuine stress responses that a global stress-score regression or filter would remove, and drug calls that are really handling artefacts
gain: none measured; handling time alone changed 1,185 PBMC genes (Massoni-Badosa 2020) and enzymatic digestion created a stress cluster (Marsh 2022)
caveats: Needs vehicle controls in every lane or plate and matched handling time; cultured lines have less dissociation stress than tissue but trypsinisation and wait times still apply.

name: SingleCellMQC
summary: R package for QC at sample, cell, feature and batch level across scRNA-seq, antibody-derived tags and TCR/BCR data, combining fixed thresholds, tissue-specific reference ranges and data-driven outliers in an HTML report
recovers: one QC pass over all modalities, so a cell is not dropped for one modality's failure without that being visible
gain: demonstrated on a 28,498-cell PBMC multi-omics dataset, a 137,214-cell PBMC dataset and a breast atlas of over 1 million cells; no comparison of cells retained
caveats: New (2026); built on Seurat and BPCells; its ADT doublet and threshold choices have not been independently evaluated.
cite_title: SingleCellMQC: A comprehensive quality control workflow for single-cell multi-omics
publication_title: SingleCellMQC: A comprehensive quality control workflow for single-cell multi-omics

name: SpatialArtifacts
summary: Finds spatially contiguous tissue artefacts (dry patches, tissue lifting, uneven reagent) in Visium and VisiumHD by combining MAD outliers with morphological operations and classifying them as edge or interior, large or small
recovers: none; removes or flags artefact regions for review while keeping true low-count domains
gain: demonstrated on human hippocampus, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and colorectal cancer; no counts in the abstract
caveats: Preprint (2026).
cite_title: SpatialArtifacts: a computational framework for tissue artifact detection in spatial transcriptomics data
publication_title: SpatialArtifacts: a computational framework for tissue artifact detection in spatial transcriptomics data

name: Stealth multiplets in sample multiplexing (Nakaki & Sharpe 2025)
summary: Models four classes of multiplet in sample-multiplexed droplet data (homogeneous stealth, partial stealth, multilabelled, unlabelled) and shows partial-stealth multiplets, where one cell's label is lost, in real hashed and genotype-pooled datasets
gain: none (cautionary finding)
caveats: Probabilities are model-based; partial-stealth multiplets matter most when labelling or demultiplexing is weak.
cite_title: Probability of stealth multiplets in sample-multiplexing for droplet-based single-cell analysis
publication_title: Probability of stealth multiplets in sample-multiplexing for droplet-based single-cell analysis

name: Stress-altered transcription gene panels (Yan 2026)
summary: Tissue-specific dissociation-stress gene panels for brain and skull bone marrow, refined by random forest from paired gentle and conventional preparations, used to detect and remove the artefact retrospectively
recovers: published datasets prepared with conventional dissociation
gain: the optimised protocol cut stress-altered transcription by about 95%; the panels alone cut it by 60-64% (self-reported)
caveats: Neuroimmune tissues only; repository not checked.
cite_title: A two-pronged strategy eliminates dissociation artifacts for high-fidelity neuroimmune single-cell transcriptomics
publication_title: A two-pronged strategy eliminates dissociation artifacts for high-fidelity neuroimmune single-cell transcriptomics

name: Superloading with sample multiplexing
summary: Loading a droplet lane well above the standard concentration when cells carry sample tags or genotypes, so cross-sample multiplets are removed and more singlets are kept per lane
recovers: singlets per lane and per unit cost
gain: scPower cost-power model (independent of the hashing authors): with doublet detection, overloading lanes raised DE and eQTL power under a fixed budget even after doublets were discarded; Cell Hashing (self-reported, modelled): about 4x more singlets at a matched unresolved multiplet rate
caveats: Needs either tags or genotypes; same-sample multiplets stay undetected (about 1/N of multiplets for N equal samples); Mylka 2022 saw 48% more captured cells give 125% more doublets and 325% more unassigned barcodes; scPower notes observed doublet rates above its model, so modelled gains are upper bounds; calling with [[demuxlet]], [[htodemux]] or similar T1 tools

name: Tag-guided rescue of low-RNA cells
summary: Using a confident sample tag as independent evidence that a barcode holds a cell, to keep low-RNA barcodes that RNA-only cell calling or UMI floors would discard
recovers: cells with little RNA (neutrophils, small or stressed cells) below the usual UMI cut-off
gain: Self-reported in MULTI-seq: in cryopreserved PDX samples, 90.8% of sequenced neutrophils were below the CellRanger UMI inflection (1 350) and were kept because their barcodes classified; low-RNA barcodes that did not classify looked like broken cells
caveats: Free or ambient tags can make debris droplets look tagged, so a tag floor plus RNA checks are still needed; hashing negatives had ~2x fewer UMIs than singlets (Mylka 2022), so tag and RNA failure partly co-occur; no independent benchmark
cite_title: MULTI-seq: sample multiplexing for single-cell RNA sequencing using lipid-tagged indices.
publication_title: MULTI-seq: sample multiplexing for single-cell RNA sequencing using lipid-tagged indices.

name: ULMnet
summary: Scores each barcode against cell-type marker signatures with univariate linear models to identify multiplets, predict their composition and build physical cell-cell interaction networks
recovers: multiplet composition and contact networks from routine and partially dissociated scRNA-seq
gain: FACS-sorted DC-T doublets: sensitivity 56% in vitro and 39% in vivo at 99.7-99.9% precision, against 52.1%/29.2% for Neighbor-seq and 21.7%/15.1% for CIcADA
caveats: comparison run by the method's own authors on two sorted-doublet datasets; sensitivity drops in vivo; no packaged repository named in the paper (built on decoupleR run_ulm)
cite_title: ULMnet: inferring physical cell-cell communication networks from scRNAseq data using univariate linear models
publication_title: ULMnet: inferring physical cell-cell communication networks from scRNAseq data using univariate linear models

name: Well-to-well null from replicate control wells
summary: Compare each drug-vs-vehicle statistic (DE count, effect distance, program shift) with its distribution across vehicle-vs-vehicle well pairs, so the significance threshold reflects real culture-to-culture variation
recovers: Calibrated calls in screens where most conditions have one well, using the null-comparison logic of the Squair 2021 and Junttila 2022 mock analyses
caveats: Needs several vehicle wells spread across plates and positions; assumes drug wells vary like vehicle wells; summary statistics must be computed identically (same cell numbers, subsampled if needed). Not validated in a published drug screen.

name: Xoublet
summary: Scrublet-like doublet scoring with a hierarchical tree for fast neighbour search, built for atlas-scale data
gain: 2,479,674 HeartMap profiles scored in 574.8 s and 4.14 GiB peak memory against 1060.6 s and 22.81 GiB for the Scrublet core (self-reported)
caveats: Its own paper reports accuracy similar to Scrublet on cell-line hashing data but less discriminative on human-mouse and PBMC benchmarks.
cite_title: Xoublet: An Extreme-Scale Doublet Detection Algorithm for Cardiac Single-Cell Transcriptomics
publication_title: Xoublet: An Extreme-Scale Doublet Detection Algorithm for Cardiac Single-Cell Transcriptomics
